definition_zh: 联合；结合；工会；联盟；同盟；团结
definition_en: the joining of separate parts into one, or an organization formed by such a joining
core_image: 两只手握在一起，指尖扣得紧紧的
scene: 十几家小作坊的师傅在一张桌前签下同一份章程，从此一起谈价钱。 The craftsmen formed a union to protect their trade.
sceneCN: 这里 union 是「工会」（第 2 个义项：由联合而成的组织）；句意为工匠们结成了一个行会来维护本行。两只紧握的手，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「联合；团结」
同根名词，义为「团结；统一」
动词加 -ed 的形容词，义为「联合的；一致的」
同根动词，义为「统一；使一致」

senses.title: The act of joining into one
senses.definition: the joining of two or more things so that they become one
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多事物结合成一体的过程
senses.example: The bridge is a happy union of steel and glass.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥是钢与玻璃的巧妙结合。
senses.why: The Latin unus, one, plus the noun ending io, gives the idea of making one out of several.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 unus（一）加名词词尾 io，给出「把多个变成一」的意思。

senses.title: An organization of workers
senses.definition: an organization of employees who act together over pay and conditions
senses.definitionCN: 为工资与工作条件共同行动的雇员组织
senses.example: The union asked for a shorter working week.
senses.exampleCN: 工会要求缩短每周工作时间。
senses.why: Workers who speak with one voice are joined into one body, and the body takes the name.
senses.whyCN: 用一个声音说话的工人被联结成一个整体，而这个整体直接取得了这个名字。

senses.title: A league of states or groups
senses.definition: a political or trade alliance in which separate parts keep some of their own powers
senses.definitionCN: 各部分保留部分自主权的政治或经济联盟
senses.example: The two countries signed a customs union in 1957.
senses.exampleCN: 两国在 1957 年签订了一个关税同盟。
senses.why: Joining for a purpose without melting completely is the political version of the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 为了某个目的结合而不完全融为一体，是同一幅画面的政治版本。

senses.title: Harmony between people
senses.definition: a state of agreement and love between people or within a group
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间或群体内部的和谐与情谊
senses.example: The couple lived in union for fifty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妻和睦地生活了五十年。
senses.why: When separate lives hold together, the union is a bond rather than an institution.
senses.whyCN: 当各自的生活握在一起，这个 union 就是一种纽带，而不是机构。

senses.title: A place where students gather
senses.definition: used in names of student organizations or their buildings
senses.definitionCN: 用于学生组织或其活动场所的名称
senses.example: They met at the student union and planned the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在学生会见面，筹划了那场音乐会。
senses.why: A building named after the joining of students is simply the institution turned into a place.
senses.whyCN: 以学生之联合命名的场所，不过是把机构变成了具体的地方。

intro.en: The word goes back to Latin unio, oneness, from unus, one.
intro.cn: 这个词可追到拉丁语 unio（一体），源自 unus（一）。

items.en: Unio meant oneness, and also named a single large pearl.
items.cn: unio 意为「一体」，也指一颗大珍珠。

items.en: The word entered French as union with the sense of combining.
items.cn: 该词进入法语作 union，含「结合」之义。

items.en: English used union for the joining of things, people, and realms.
items.cn: 英语用 union 表示物、人与人乃至王国的结合。

items.en: From the eighteenth century it named associations of workers or traders.
items.cn: 十八世纪起，它用来指工人或商人的组织。

items.en: In politics it appears in the names of alliances and federal states.
items.cn: 在政治中，它出现于联盟与联邦国家的名称里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers uni- words, and the near-meaning group covers leagues and harmony.
note.cn: 形近组收集 uni- 开头的词，近义组覆盖联盟与和谐的说法。

the state of being one
one shared dress
a round vegetable with layers

normalIntro.en: One root, one, sits under the union, the unit, and the united.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「一」的词根，撑起 union、unit 与 united。

normal.en: Uni- is one, and -ion makes a noun of the joining.
normal.cn: uni- 是「一」，-ion 把这种结合变作名词。

normal.en: Trade union is the British phrase; labor union is the American one.
normal.cn: trade union 是英式说法，labor union 是美式说法。

normal.en: Unity is the state, union is the act or the body.
normal.cn: unity 是状态，union 是行为或那个实体。

normal.en: United appears in country names that grew out of unions.
normal.cn: 许多国家名里的 united 正出自这样的联合。

normal.en: The same root gives unit, unite, and unique.
normal.cn: 同一个词根还生出 unit、unite 与 unique。

abstract.en: Picture two hands clasped with fingers locked.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手指紧扣的手。

abstract.en: See dozens of small workshops putting one stamp on a single sheet.
abstract.cn: 看几十家小作坊在同一张纸上盖下同一个印。

abstract.en: Hear a hall of voices agreeing on a single sentence.
abstract.cn: 听满厅的声音在同一句话上达成一致。

examples.en: The union of the two firms created the largest bank in the region.
examples.cn: 两家公司的合并造就了本地区最大的银行。

examples.en: Union members voted to accept the new pay offer.
examples.cn: 工会会员投票接受了新的薪酬方案。

examples.en: Their marriage was a union of two very different families.
examples.cn: 他们的婚姻是两个差异极大的家庭的结合。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尤尼昂」——尤尼（一）加昂（上），大家往一个方向上凑，就是联合。

root: 拉丁语 unus（一）+ 名词词尾 -io 构成 unio（一体），经古法语 union 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One root, one, gives the act of joining, the body formed, the league, the bond, and the building.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个表示「一」的词根，给出结合的行为、形成的实体、联盟、纽带与场所。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands clasped with fingers locked.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手指紧扣的手。

branches.en: The act branch: things joined into a new whole.
branches.cn: 行为分支：事物联结成新的整体。

branches.en: The workers branch: one voice for many employees.
branches.cn: 劳工分支：众多雇员共用一个声音。

branches.en: The state branch: separate parts under one flag.
branches.cn: 国家分支：各部分共处一面旗帜之下。

branches.en: The bond branch: lives held together in harmony.
branches.cn: 纽带分支：和谐中相依的生活。

branches.en: The place branch: a building named after the joining.
branches.cn: 场所分支：以这种联合命名的建筑。

intro.en: The word is a Latin number plus a noun ending, carried through French.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语数词加名词词尾，经由法语传来。

latinIntro.en: Unus and unio are the Latin sources, and uni- recurs across the family.
latinIntro.cn: unus 与 unio 是拉丁语来源，uni- 在这一族里反复出现。

definition_zh: 提高；增强；提升价值
definition_en: to improve the quality, strength, or value of something
core_image: 把一件东西一点点垫高，让它在光线下显得更亮、更有分量
scene: 新来的教练没有换掉旧战术，只是把训练强度一点点提上去，球队的速度明显变快。 The new coach enhanced the team's speed with small daily drills.
sceneCN: 这里 enhance 是「提高；增强」（第 1 个义项：改善质量或水平）；句意：新教练通过每天的小训练提高了球队的速度。

derivatives.zh: 提高；增强
增强剂；增强器
增强的；提高的

senses.title: To improve quality
senses.definition: to make something better in quality, usefulness, or appearance
senses.definitionCN: 使某物在质量、实用性或外观上变得更好
senses.example: The new windows enhance the look of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 新窗户提升了房子的外观。
senses.why: The word comes from a root meaning high, so enhancing is lifting something to a higher standard.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自意为「高」的词根，所以 enhance 就是把某物提升到更高的水准。

senses.title: To increase strength or degree
senses.definition: to increase the strength, effect, or amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 增加某物的强度、效果或数量
senses.example: Regular exercise enhances the body's ability to resist illness.
senses.exampleCN: 规律运动增强身体抵抗疾病的能力。
senses.why: Lifting something higher also means raising its intensity, which gives the sense of strengthening.
senses.whyCN: 把某物抬得更高也意味着提高其强度，于是产生「加强」这一义项。

senses.title: To raise value
senses.definition: to increase the money or social value of something
senses.definitionCN: 提高某物的金钱价值或社会价值
senses.example: The restoration enhanced the value of the old building.
senses.exampleCN: 这次修复提升了这栋老建筑的价值。
senses.why: If quality rises, the price or worth people assign to it can rise too.
senses.whyCN: 如果质量提高，人们赋予它的价格或价值也会随之上升。

intro.en: Enhance comes through Old French enhaucier from Vulgar Latin altiare, to raise, from Latin altus, high.
intro.cn: enhance 经古法语 enhaucier 来自俗拉丁语 altiare（抬高），其根源是拉丁语 altus（高的）。

items.en: Altus means high or deep, and it also gives English altitude.
items.cn: altus 意为高的或深的，也是英语 altitude 的来源。

items.en: Altiare means to make high or raise up.
items.cn: altiare 意为使变高、抬高。

items.en: Old French enhaucier adds en- and means to raise or exalt.
items.cn: 古法语 enhaucier 加上 en-，意为抬高或提升。

items.en: The French verb crosses into English law and courtly writing.
items.cn: 这个法语动词进入英语的法律与宫廷写作。

items.en: Middle English enhance means to raise in rank, value, or dignity.
items.cn: 中古英语 enhance 指提高等级、价值或尊严。

items.en: Modern English widens the word to quality, performance, and effect.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义扩展到质量、表现和效果。

note.en: Enhance belongs to a family about making something better or higher, and it sits near words for improving and increasing.
note.cn: enhance 属于「使某物更好或更高」的词族，与改善和增加类词相邻。

something that improves or strengthens an effect
improved or increased

normalIntro.en: Enhance sounds like in hance, and the image is lifting something higher, which matches its Latin root for high.
normalIntro.cn: enhance 读起来像 in hance，画面是把东西往高处抬，这正对应它表示「高」的拉丁词根。

normal.en: The en- at the front means make or put into, so enhance is to put something into a higher state.
normal.cn: 开头的 en- 表示「使、置入」，所以 enhance 就是使某物进入更高的状态。

normal.en: Enhance the quality is the most common pattern in modern writing.
normal.cn: enhance the quality 是现代写作中最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Enhance and improvement belong together: the verb and the noun.
normal.cn: enhance 与 improvement 相配：一个是动词，一个是名词。

normal.en: The ending -ment in enhancement turns the action into a noun.
normal.cn: enhancement 中的 -ment 把动作变成名词。

normal.en: Compare increase: increase is about amount, enhance is about quality or value.
normal.cn: 对比 increase：increase 侧重数量，enhance 侧重质量或价值。

abstract.en: Picture a painting lit from below so its colours seem richer.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅画从下方打光，颜色显得更饱满。

abstract.en: Imagine a sound system turned up just enough to fill the room.
abstract.cn: 想象音响被调到刚好填满房间的程度。

abstract.en: Think of a rough stone polished until its pattern shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一块粗石被磨亮，纹理显现出来。

examples.en: Good lighting can enhance the colours in a photograph.
examples.cn: 好的光线能增强照片里的色彩。

examples.en: The course is designed to enhance students' writing skills.
examples.cn: 这门课程旨在提高学生的写作能力。

examples.en: A famous tenant enhanced the reputation of the building.
examples.cn: 一位有名气的租户提升了这栋楼的声誉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「恩汉斯」——恩惠把水平往上抬，就是提高；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 altus（高的）→ 俗拉丁语 altiare（抬高）→ 古法语 enhaucier → 中古英语 enhance，本义「抬高、提升」，后指提高质量与价值。

sensesIntro.en: Lifting something higher gives three results: better quality, greater strength, and higher value.
sensesIntro.cn: 把某物抬得更高带来三种结果：质量更好、强度更大、价值更高。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something lifted to a higher level so that it shows better.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物被抬到更高的层次，因而显得更好。

branches.en: Improving quality is the most general modern sense.
branches.cn: 提高质量，是最概括的现代义项。

branches.en: Raising intensity gives the sense of strengthening.
branches.cn: 提高强度，产生「加强」这一义项。

branches.en: Raising worth gives the sense of increasing value.
branches.cn: 提高价值，产生「增值」这一义项。

branches.en: Better quality and higher value usually rise together.
branches.cn: 质量更好与价值更高通常一起上升。

branches.en: Strength and value both measure the higher level the thing has reached.
branches.cn: 强度与价值都衡量事物所达到的更高水平。

intro.en: Enhance is a French-shaped verb built on a Latin root for high, with English endings forming its family.
intro.cn: enhance 是法语形态的动词，建立在表示「高」的拉丁词根上，其词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin altus means high, and altiare means to raise, which becomes enhaucier in French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 altus 表示高，altiare 表示抬高，在法语中变成 enhaucier。

definition_zh: 出奇地；令人惊讶地；出乎意料地

core_image: 一个难题旁画着对勾，答题者自己都不敢相信
scene: 这次考试出奇地容易。 The test was surprisingly easy for everyone.

senses.whyCN: 作句子副词时评论整个陈述。

senses.example: Soil organic matter feeds the whole food web.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤有机物养活了整个食物网。
senses.why: Greek organon named a tool, and a body's tools are its organs; 'organic' therefore starts as 'having organs', that is, belonging to a living body.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 organon 指工具，而身体的工具就是器官；因此 organic 起初意为「有器官的」，即属于活体。

senses.title: Carbon-based chemistry
senses.titleCN: 有机化学义：含碳骨架的化合物
senses.definition: describing compounds built on carbon skeletons, the chemistry once thought to require life
senses.definitionCN: 描述以碳骨架为基础的化合物，这一化学领域曾被以为只能由生命产生
senses.example: Methane is the simplest organic compound.
senses.exampleCN: 甲烷是最简单的有机化合物。
senses.why: because such compounds were first obtained only from living things, the word was carried over to the whole class even after they were synthesized in the lab.
senses.whyCN: 由于这类化合物最初只能从生物得到，即使后来能在实验室合成，这个词仍被沿用到整类物质上。

senses.title: Grown without synthetics
senses.titleCN: 农业义：不用化肥农药的
senses.definition: describing food grown without synthetic pesticides or soluble mineral fertilizers
senses.definitionCN: 描述不用合成农药或可溶矿物肥料的种植方式
senses.example: Organic apples cost more because the orchard yields less.
senses.exampleCN: 有机苹果更贵，因为果园产量更低。
senses.why: the farming sense borrows the idea of a whole living system, treating the soil as something to be fed rather than dosed.
senses.whyCN: 农业义借用「活着的整体系统」这一观念，把土壤当作需要喂养的东西，而不是投药的对象。

senses.title: Grown as a whole, not assembled
senses.titleCN: 演化义：自然生长、整体关联的
senses.definition: describing something that develops naturally as an interconnected whole rather than being assembled from parts
senses.definitionCN: 描述作为相互关联的整体自然发展，而非由零件拼装
senses.example: The firm's growth was organic, not the result of acquisitions.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司的增长是自然生长，而非并购的结果。
senses.why: since the body grows from within, 'organic' also means growth by inner development rather than by outside assembly, and business borrowed that.
senses.whyCN: 由于身体是从内部长成的，organic 也指由内在发展而非外部拼装的成长，商业领域借用了这一层。

senses.title: Of the organs in medicine
senses.definition: describing disease that has a structural change in an organ rather than a purely functional one
senses.definitionCN: 描述器官有结构改变、而非纯功能性的疾病
senses.example: The scan ruled out organic disease of the stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描排除了胃的器质性病变。
senses.why: medicine must separate damage to an organ from symptoms without a lesion, so 'organic' marks the structural case.
senses.whyCN: 医学必须把器官的结构损伤与无病灶的症状分开，因此 organic 标记结构性的那一类。

senses.title: Parts that belong together
senses.titleCN: 结构义：组织上相互关联的
senses.definition: describing a structure whose parts are interdependent, like the organs of a body
senses.definitionCN: 描述各部分相互依赖的结构，如同身体的器官
senses.example: The report describes an organic link between the two agencies.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把两个机构之间的关系描述为有机联系。
senses.why: if organs serve one body, then any set of parts serving one end can be called organic.
senses.whyCN: 如果各器官服务于同一个身体，那么任何共赴一目的的一组部件都可以叫 organic。

senses.title: Foundational law and acts
senses.titleCN: 根本性义：作为根本法规的
senses.definition: describing a basic constitutional document or act, as in organic law
senses.definitionCN: 描述根本性的宪制文件或法令，如「组织法」
senses.example: The status of the territory is set by an organic act.
senses.exampleCN: 该领地的地位由一部组织法规定。
senses.why: a body needs a skeleton, so a state's founding instrument is called organic: it is what the rest is built onto.
senses.whyCN: 身体需要骨骼，因此国家的立国文件被称为「有机的」：其余一切都建在它之上。

senses.title: Whole food, whole system
senses.titleCN: 食品义：作为整体未被拆解的
senses.definition: describing food or a system treated as an intact whole rather than as isolated components
senses.definitionCN: 描述被当作完整整体、而非孤立成分处理的食品或系统
senses.example: The shop sells organics alongside conventional produce.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店把有机产品与常规农产品并排出售。
senses.why: the market turned the adjective into a noun, so 'organics' now names the goods themselves.
senses.whyCN: 市场把这个形容词变成名词，因此 organics 现在指商品本身。

intro.en: Organic comes from Greek organon 'tool, instrument', through Latin organum and the medieval adjective organicus. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: organic 出自希腊 organon「工具、器具」，经拉丁 organum 与中世纪形容词 organicus 而来。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: organon named a tool or instrument, and in philosophy a means of doing something. From it comes the sense of a body part that does work.
items.cn: organon 指工具或器具，也指哲学上达成某目的的手段。由它引申出「做工作的身体部件」这一义。

items.en: Latin borrowed organum for an instrument and, in later use, a musical instrument; the body-part sense developed in anatomy.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 organum 指器具，后亦指乐器；身体部件的义项在解剖学中发展起来。

items.en: Medieval Latin organicus meant 'of an organ' or 'having organs'; English took the adjective in this anatomical sense first.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 organicus 意为「器官的」或「有器官的」；英语先在这个解剖学意义上使用该形容词。

items.en: Around 1800 chemists divided compounds into organic, from living things, and inorganic; urea's laboratory synthesis in 1828 weakened the boundary but the name stayed.
items.cn: 约 1800 年，化学家把化合物分为来自生物的 organic 与 inorganic；1828 年尿素在实验室被合成，动摇了这条界线，但名称保留。

items.en: The twentieth century applied the word to farming that avoids synthetic inputs, treating soil as a living system.
items.cn: 20 世纪把这个词用于避免合成投入物的耕作方式，把土壤当作活系统。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): organon's pre-Greek origin is not established, so any Indo-European form behind it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：organon 在希腊语之前的来源并无定论，其背后的任何印欧形式都是重构，而非有记录的实际词。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Greek stem that name different things; group two holds words often used where organic could be chosen.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊词干、但指不同事物的词；第二组是常与 organic 互换使用的词。

entries.definition: A part of a body or an organisation, not a quality; organic is the adjective describing such a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体或机构的部件，不是性质；organic 是描述这类整体的形容词。

entries.definition: A complete living being; it shares organon but names an entity, not a property.
entries.definitionCN: 指完整的生物体；共享 organon，但命名实体而非性质。

entries.definition: A structured group of people, from the same stem via 'organize'. It names an institution, not a growing whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指有结构的人群，由同一词干经 organize 而来；命名机构，不是生长的整体。

entries.definition: Not built on carbon and not from life; it is the direct opposite in chemistry and farming.
entries.definitionCN: 不以碳为基础、非来自生命；在化学与农业中与 organic 直接相对。

entries.definition: Not made or altered by humans; organic in farming also implies natural methods, but natural says nothing about certification.
entries.definitionCN: 非人力制造或改动的；农业中的 organic 也含自然方式，但 natural 不涉及认证。

entries.definition: Relating to biology or to living processes; it names the science, while organic names a property of matter.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物学或生命过程相关；命名学科，而 organic 命名物质属性。

entries.definition: Good for health or morally sound; organic food is often called wholesome, but the words answer different questions.
entries.definitionCN: 有益健康或品德端正；有机食品常被称 wholesome，但两词回答不同问题。

entries.definition: Arranged by an outside plan; organic growth is the opposite of planned assembly.
entries.definitionCN: 按外部方案安排；organic growth 恰与计划拼装相反。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek organon 'tool': a body's tools are its organs, so organic first means 'having organs'.
normal.cn: 希腊 organon「工具」：身体的工具就是器官，所以 organic 起初意为「有器官的」。

normal.en: The family runs organ, organism, organization, organic, organically, inorganic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 organ、organism、organization、organic、organically、inorganic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: organic matter, organic compound, organic farming, organic growth, organic chemistry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：有机物、有机化合物、有机农业、自然增长、有机化学。

normal.en: Chemistry pairs it with inorganic; farming pairs it with conventional.
normal.cn: 化学中与 inorganic 相对；农业中与常规耕作相对。

normal.en: The business sense is 'grown from within', the opposite of bought through acquisitions.
normal.cn: 商业义是「从内部长成」，与靠并购得来相反。

abstract.en: Picture a plant whose root, stem and leaf all serve one life.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物，根、茎、叶都服务于同一条生命。

abstract.en: Picture a city that grew along its roads instead of being stamped out at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市沿道路长出来，而不是一次压印成形。

abstract.en: Picture a table whose legs are not attached but grown from the same wood.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，桌腿不是装上去的，而是与桌面同一块木料长出来的。

examples.en: Organic matter in the soil holds water between grains.
examples.cn: 土壤中的有机物在颗粒之间持水。

examples.en: Organic chemistry began with compounds isolated from plants and animals.
examples.cn: 有机化学始于从动植物中分离出的化合物。

examples.en: The company preferred organic growth to borrowing for acquisitions.
examples.cn: 公司更愿自然增长，而不是借钱并购。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「有器官（organ）的」——凡活物长成的、含碳的、不用化肥的 → 有机的

root: 希腊 organon「工具、器具」→ 拉丁 organum → 中世纪拉丁 organicus「有器官的」→ 英语 organic；19 世纪扩展为化学义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: a body's parts all serve one life; that image is read as living matter, as carbon chemistry, as chemical-free farming, as growth from within, as structural disease, as interdependence, as a founding law, and as goods sold under that label.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个意象展开：身体的各部分都服务于同一条生命；这一意象依次被读成生命物质、碳化学、无合成投入的耕作、由内生长、器质性疾病、相互依赖、立国根本法，以及以此标签出售的商品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: root, stem and leaf all serving one living whole, with nothing bolted on.
core.cn: 核心意象：根、茎、叶都服务于同一个活的整体，没有一件是外装的。

branches.en: LIVING MATTER: the oldest sense, matter that belongs to a body.
branches.cn: 生命物质：最古老的义项，属于身体的物质。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY: the carbon class, named when such compounds came only from life.
branches.cn: 化学：碳化合物这一类，命名时它们只来自生命。

branches.en: FARMING AND GOODS: soil fed as a living system, and produce sold as organics.
branches.cn: 农业与商品：把土壤当活系统来养，以及作为 organic 产品出售。

branches.en: GROWTH: development from within, borrowed by business for unplanned expansion.
branches.cn: 生长：由内发展，商业借指非计划性扩张。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: organ damage in medicine, interdependent parts, and a state's founding law.
branches.cn: 结构：医学上的器官损伤、相互依赖的部件，以及国家的立国根本法。

intro.en: Organic is Greek organon plus the Latin adjectival ending -icus, kept in English as -ic; the family also uses -ism and -ize.
intro.cn: organic 是希腊 organon 加拉丁形容词词尾 -icus，在英语中保留为 -ic；词族还用 -ism 与 -ize。

latinIntro.en: Latin organum is a borrowed Greek word, and medieval organicus is a Latin formation on it; both are real Latin, though the root is Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 organum 是借自希腊语的词，中世纪 organicus 是在其上形成的拉丁词；二者都是真实的拉丁语，但词根属希腊语。

items.meaning: of organs, of living things; carbon-based
a body part that does work
items.example: The liver is the largest internal organ.
items.exampleCN: 肝脏是最大的内部器官。

items.example: A single organism can be a whole forest patch.
items.exampleCN: 单个生物体可以是一整片林地。

items.meaningCN: 非碳基的、非来自生命的
items.example: Inorganic salts dissolve in the water.

items.meaning: dead or living material from organisms
items.meaningCN: 来自生物的活或死的物质

items.example: Organic chemistry began with natural products.
items.exampleCN: 有机化学始于天然产物。

items.meaning: a small organ of a cell

latinEntries.structure: organum, organi (n., second declension; Greek loanword)

definition_zh: 逮捕；拘留；阻止；抑制；吸引（注意）；心脏骤停
definition_en: to seize someone by legal authority, to stop something from continuing, to catch and hold attention, or a sudden stop of the heart
core_image: 一只手从背后按住正要离开的人的肩膀
scene: 巷口的警笛声还没停，两名警员已经堵住了翻墙男子的退路。 The officers arrested the man before he could climb the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 arrest 是「逮捕、拘留」（第 1 个义项：依法抓捕某人）；句意为「警员在那名男子翻上墙之前就逮捕了他」。画面中有巷口、警笛与翻墙的人。

pos.zh: 动词：逮捕；拘留；阻止；抑制；吸引（注意）
名词：逮捕；被捕；心脏骤停

derivatives.zh: 由 arrest 加 -ee 构成，义为「被逮捕者」
由前缀 re- 加 arrest 构成，义为「再次逮捕」
由 arrest 加 -ing 构成，义为「引人注目的」

senses.title: To seize someone by legal authority
senses.definition: to take hold of someone and place them in legal custody, usually on a charge
senses.definitionCN: 抓住某人并将其置于合法羁押之下，通常因某项指控
senses.example: The officers arrested the man before he could climb the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 警员在那名男子翻上墙之前就逮捕了他。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to make something stand still, and a person is made to stop by being held.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是「使停住」，而人被抓住，就是被强制停下。

senses.title: To stop something from continuing
senses.definition: to stop or slow the course of something such as growth, decay, or movement
senses.definitionCN: 使增长、衰退或运动等过程停下或变慢
senses.example: The new treatment arrested the spread of the infection.
senses.exampleCN: 新的治疗抑制了感染的扩散。
senses.why: Here the object is not a person but a process, and arrest means to make that process stand still.
senses.whyCN: 这里被抓住的不是人而是一个过程，arrest 就是让这个过程停住不动。

senses.title: To catch and hold attention
senses.definition: to attract and hold someone's attention or interest strongly
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地吸引并留住某人的注意力或兴趣
senses.example: Her unusual story arrested everyone's attention.
senses.exampleCN: 她不寻常的经历吸引了所有人的注意。
senses.why: Attention is caught the way a hand catches an arm: once held, it cannot easily move away.
senses.whyCN: 注意力被抓住的方式，就像手抓住手臂：一旦被握住，便不容易移开。

senses.title: A sudden stop of the heart
senses.definition: in cardiac arrest, a condition in which the heart suddenly stops pumping blood
senses.definitionCN: 用于 cardiac arrest，指心脏突然停止泵血的状态
senses.example: A sudden cardiac arrest left him unconscious for several minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 一次突发的心脏骤停让他失去意识好几分钟。
senses.why: The medical phrase takes the plain sense of stopping: the organ simply stands still.
senses.whyCN: 医学短语用的是最朴素的「停住」义：这个器官就是停在那里不动了。

senses.title: The state of being held by police
senses.definition: in the phrase under arrest, the state of being held by the police
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 under arrest，指被警方羁押的状态
senses.example: The suspect remained under arrest until the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 嫌疑人一直被拘留到听证会举行。
senses.why: The noun names the condition that results once the hand has stopped the person.
senses.whyCN: 名词指的是手把人停住之后所形成的状态。

intro.en: Arrest goes back to a Latin verb for standing still, and every modern sense still carries that idea of being stopped.
intro.cn: arrest 可追到一个表示「站住」的拉丁动词，现代各个义项都还带着「被停住」的意思。

items.en: The root 「*sta-」 meant 'to stand', and it lies behind many Latin words for standing and staying.
items.cn: 词根「*sta-」意为「站立」，拉丁语中许多表示站立与停留的词都由它而来。

items.en: Restare meant 'to remain standing, stay behind'; ad- added the sense of moving toward that stopping point.
items.cn: restare 意为「继续站着、留在后面」，ad- 又添上「朝那个停点靠过去」的意思。

items.en: Arrestare is recorded in the sense 'to stop, hold back', and this is the form that passed into French.
items.cn: arrestare 有「使停下、扣住」的用法，进入法语的就是这一形式。

items.en: Arester meant both 'to stop' and 'to seize', and English took over both.
items.cn: arester 既指「停下」，也指「抓住」，英语把两义一并接收。

items.en: The legal sense of holding a person is recorded early, and the medical phrase cardiac arrest comes much later.
items.cn: 扣押某人的法律义很早就出现，医学术语 cardiac arrest 则要晚得多。

items.en: The word now covers police custody, halted processes, held attention and a stopped heart.
items.cn: 这个词如今涵盖警方羁押、被止住的过程、被抓住的注意力，以及停跳的心脏。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short verbs close to arrest in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of seizing, detaining and stopping.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写与 arrest 接近的短动词；近义组收表示抓住、扣留与阻止的动词。

entries.definition: A verb or noun for stopping activity and relaxing, from the same Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「休息」，与 arrest 同出拉丁词根。

entries.definition: To state something firmly as true.
To show or declare that something is true or genuine.
To keep someone in official custody, often while a case is examined.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人置于官方扣留之下，常在案件审查期间。

entries.definition: To take someone or something by force.
entries.definitionCN: 以武力抓住某人或某物。

entries.definition: To take hold of something quickly and firmly.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速而有力地抓住某物。

entries.definition: To stop, or to cause something to stop.

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a hand on the shoulder to halted growth, held attention and a stopped heart.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从按在肩上的手，走到被止住的增长、被抓住的注意力与停跳的心脏。

normal.en: A hand on the shoulder: the person is made to stand still.
normal.cn: 一只手按在肩上：这个人被迫站住。

normal.en: Police arrest: the state stops the person's movement.
normal.cn: 警方逮捕：国家让这个人不能再走动。

normal.en: Arrest a process: growth stands still.
normal.cn: 抑制一个过程：增长停在那里。

normal.en: Arrest attention: the eyes stop and turn.
normal.cn: 吸引注意：目光停住并转过来。

normal.en: Cardiac arrest: the heart itself stops.
normal.cn: 心脏骤停：心脏本身停了下来。

abstract.en: The core idea is making something stand still.
abstract.cn: 核心意思是让某样东西停住不动。

abstract.en: The same word stops people, processes, eyes and a heart.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能让人的脚步、进程、目光乃至心脏停下。

abstract.en: Legal custody is only one form of that stopping.
abstract.cn: 法律上的羁押只是这种「停住」的一种形式。

examples.en: The officers arrested the man before he could climb the wall.
examples.cn: 警员在那名男子翻上墙之前就逮捕了他。

examples.en: A sudden cardiac arrest left him unconscious for several minutes.
examples.cn: 一次突发的心脏骤停让他失去意识好几分钟。

examples.en: Her unusual story arrested everyone's attention.
examples.cn: 她不寻常的经历吸引了所有人的注意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿瑞斯特」——阿瑞斯特在巷口被警员按住肩膀，动弹不得：逮捕

root: arrest 来自拉丁语 ad-（向）加 restare（停住、站住），俗拉丁语 arrestare 意为「使停下」，经古法语 arester 进入英语。本义是让人或物停住，于是有了三层引申：让人停下就是逮捕，让过程停下就是抑制，让目光停下就是吸引注意；医学术语 cardiac arrest 则是心脏本身停跳。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses share one core: making something stand still. A person is held, a process is halted, attention is caught, the heart stops, and custody is the state that follows.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项共享一个核心：让某样东西停住。人被扣住，过程被止住，注意力被抓住，心脏停跳，羁押则是停住之后的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand from behind landing on the shoulder of someone about to leave.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从背后按在正要离开的人肩上。

branches.en: THE PERSON LINE: legal arrest makes a person stand still.
branches.cn: 人身线：法律上的逮捕让人停住。

branches.en: THE PROCESS LINE: growth and spread are made to stand still.
branches.cn: 过程线：增长与扩散被止住。

branches.en: THE EYE LINE: attention is caught and held in place.
branches.cn: 目光线：注意力被抓住并固定在原处。

branches.en: THE HEART LINE: the organ itself stops pumping.
branches.cn: 心脏线：这个器官自己停止了泵血。

branches.en: THE CUSTODY LINE: once stopped, the person remains in a held state.
branches.cn: 羁押线：一旦被停住，这个人就处在被扣留的状态。

intro.en: Arrest is a Latin verb carried through French; its family adds prefixes and suffixes to the same stopping core.
intro.cn: arrest 是经法语传来的拉丁动词，它的词族围绕同一个「停住」核心加前缀与后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root restare also produced rest and restive, which keep the sense of staying or standing back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 restare 还生出 rest 与 restive，它们都保留「停留、退后」的意思。

items.example: The guard arrested the man at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 警卫在门口抓住了那名男子。

items.meaning: the third person singular or plural noun
items.example: The city reports several arrests each night.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市每晚都会报告数起逮捕。

items.meaning: the past tense and past participle
items.example: He was arrested near the station.

items.meaning: the present participle, or an adjective for something striking
items.meaningCN: 现在分词，或表示「引人注目的」形容词
items.example: The painting has an arresting colour.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画的色彩十分抓眼。

items.meaning: a person who has been arrested
items.exampleCN: 被逮捕者被拘留了一夜。

items.example: Police rearrested him after the new evidence.
items.exampleCN: 有了新证据后，警方再次逮捕了他。

items.meaning: the act of arresting, or a legal attachment of property
items.meaningCN: 逮捕行为，或法律上的财产扣押
items.example: The arrestment of the ship's cargo was disputed.
items.exampleCN: 对船货的扣押引发了争议。

items.meaning: describing an offence for which a person may be arrested
items.meaningCN: 形容可据以逮捕的罪行
items.example: It is an arrestable offence under the act.
items.exampleCN: 依该法这属于可逮捕的罪行。

latinEntries.meaning: to stop activity and stay still
latinEntries.example: They rested by the river at noon.

latinEntries.meaning: unable to stay still, restless and impatient
latinEntries.exampleCN: 躁动的人群变得越来越不安。

definition_zh: 精确地；准确地；恰恰；正好；（回答时）正是如此；严谨地
definition_en: in an exact way with no approximation; exactly at a stated point; as a firm reply of agreement; and with careful attention to every detail
core_image: 秒针压住刻度线，分毫不差，指针停在那里没有再动
scene: 站台上的人都低头看表，广播响起时，秒针正好压在整点刻度上。 The train pulled out at precisely nine o'clock, and the platform emptied within a minute.
sceneCN: 这里 precisely 指「恰好、正好在某一刻」（第 2 个义项：强调时间点分毫不差）；句意为列车恰好在九点整驶出，站台一分钟内就空了。图中可辨识场景：低头看表的人群、压在整点刻度上的秒针、迅速空下去的站台。

pos.zh: 精确地；准确地；恰恰；严谨地

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁分词 praecisus 经法语进入英语，义为「精确的；明确的」
由 precise 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「精确；精密度」
由 precise 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「精确；严谨」

senses.title: In an exact and accurate way
senses.definition: in a way that is exact in every detail and contains no approximation
senses.definitionCN: 每一个细节都准确，不含任何近似成分
senses.example: The instrument measures the temperature precisely.
senses.exampleCN: 这台仪器能精确测量温度。
senses.why: Latin praecidere meant to cut off, and its participle praecisus described something trimmed until nothing extra was left; an exact figure is exactly that, with every vague edge shaved away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praecidere 意为「切掉」，分词 praecisus 形容被削到不剩多余部分的东西；一个精确的数字正是如此，所有模糊的边角都被削掉了。

senses.title: Exactly, at one stated point
senses.definition: used to stress that something happens at exactly a stated time, place or manner and not merely near it
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调某事恰好在所说的时间、地点或方式上发生，而不是接近而已
senses.example: The power failed precisely at the moment the speech began.
senses.exampleCN: 就在演讲开始的那一刻，电停了。
senses.why: Once the word means with nothing left over, it can point to a single instant or a single spot, and the stress falls on the perfect fit between the words and the fact.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示「不留余量」，它就能指向某一个瞬间或某一个点，重音落在「话与事实严丝合缝」上。

senses.title: Exactly so, as a reply of agreement
senses.definition: used alone as a firm reply to say that the other person has understood something completely
senses.definitionCN: 单独使用，作为肯定的回答，表示对方完全理解正确
senses.example: So the delay was caused by the missing signature? Precisely.
senses.exampleCN: 所以延误是因为少了那个签名？正是如此。
senses.why: The emphatic use shrinks into a one-word answer: agreeing that a description fits perfectly is the same act as measuring a perfect fit.
senses.whyCN: 强调用法再缩成一个单词的回答：承认对方的描述完全吻合，与「量出一个严丝合缝」本是同一个动作。

senses.title: With careful attention to every detail
senses.definition: in a way that shows careful attention to small details and a strict, orderly method
senses.definitionCN: 表现出对细小环节的留意，以及严格而有条理的做法
senses.example: She recorded every reading precisely, down to the last decimal.
senses.exampleCN: 她把每个读数都记到小数点最后一位。
senses.why: Cutting away excess also describes a person's working method: whoever trims every loose detail out of an account is working precisely.
senses.whyCN: 「削去多余」也能形容一个人的做法：谁把记录里每处含糊都削干净，谁就是在严谨地做事。

senses.title: In a strict and particular manner
senses.definition: in a way that insists on exact form or correct procedure
senses.definitionCN: 以坚持确切形式或正确规程的方式
senses.example: He dresses precisely, down to the knot of his tie.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿戴讲究，连领带结都不含糊。
senses.why: The person who trims every edge applies the cut to himself, so behaviour takes the adverb.
senses.whyCN: 把每条边都削干净的人把这刀用在了自己身上，行为便用上了这个副词。

senses.title: Just, in answer of emphasis
senses.definition: used before a statement to stress that it is exactly right
senses.definitionCN: 用于陈述句前，强调所说分毫不差
senses.example: That is precisely the point I was trying to make.
senses.exampleCN: 那正是我想说的要点。
senses.why: The perfect-fit idea turns inward on language: a sentence, too, can fit the fact exactly.
senses.whyCN: 「严丝合缝」的观念转回语言本身：一句话也可以与事实恰好吻合。

senses.title: With exactness of measurement
senses.definition: by exact measurement or calculation, to a fine degree
senses.definitionCN: 以精确的测量或计算，达到很细的程度
senses.example: The engineers positioned the beam precisely by laser.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师用激光把梁精确就位。
senses.why: Instrument work is the cleanest cutting of all, so technique keeps the word at its sharpest.
senses.whyCN: 仪器作业是最干净的「切割」，技术在词义最锋利处保留了它。

senses.title: To be precise, as a discourse tag
senses.definition: in the phrase to be precisely..., used to tighten a previous remark
senses.definitionCN: 用于收紧前话，使表述更加确切
senses.example: He came late, or precisely, he came after we had finished.
senses.exampleCN: 他来晚了——确切地说，是在我们结束之后才到。
senses.why: The speaker performs the trimming aloud, cutting the rough statement to its true edge.
senses.whyCN: 说话人当着人面完成这一刀：把粗略的说法修到真实的边缘。

intro.en: Precisely is precise plus -ly, and precise goes back to a Latin verb of cutting: what is exact has had everything loose cut away.
intro.cn: precisely 是 precise 加 -ly；而 precise 可追溯到拉丁语里表示「切」的动词：所谓精确，就是把所有松散的余量都切掉。

items.en: Caedere meant to cut or to strike down, and it supplied a large number of Latin verbs about cutting, killing and deciding.
items.cn: caedere 意为切、砍倒，为拉丁语提供了大量与切割、杀戮、决断有关的动词。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or in front, whether the position was in space or in rank.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在前」，既可指空间靠前，也可指地位优先。

items.en: Praecidere joined the two: to cut off the front part, and so to shorten, to cut short, or to cut away what is extra.
items.cn: praecidere 把两者合起来：切掉前面一段，因此也表示截短、缩短、削去多余部分。

items.en: The participle praecisus meant cut off or cut short, and in learned use it came to describe a statement trimmed of everything vague.
items.cn: 分词 praecisus 意为被切掉的、被截短的，在学术用法里逐渐用来形容一段被削去所有含糊处的表述。

items.en: English borrowed precise in the sixteenth century and later added -ly; the adverb kept both the measuring sense and the emphatic one.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 precise，后来又加上 -ly；这个副词同时保留了「测量」义与「强调」义。

note.en: The look-alike group sets the adjective and its noun beside the negated form; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of accuracy and exactness.
note.cn: 形近组把本词所由来的形容词及其名词与否定式放在一起；近义组收表示准确与分毫不差的副词。

entries.definition: Exact in every detail; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 每个细节都准确；本副词所由来的形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being exact, especially in measurement or work.
entries.definitionCN: 精确的性质，尤指测量或做工上的。

entries.definition: Not exact, or not clearly stated.
The state of being exact in wording or method.
In a way that is completely correct and leaves nothing out.
In a way that is correct and free from error.
Directly and with no doubt, as in squarely in the middle.
entries.definitionCN: 正正地、毫不含糊地，如正中间。

entries.definition: With strict care and a systematic method.

normalIntro.en: The word carries a knife inside it: to be exact is to have cut away everything that does not belong to the fact.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词里藏着一把刀：所谓准确，就是把不属于事实的部分统统切掉。

normal.en: Caedere is to cut, and praecisus is cut short, so precise work is work with the loose ends removed.
normal.cn: caedere 是切，praecisus 是被截短，所以精确的活儿就是把毛边削掉的活儿。

normal.en: Precision adds -ion and names the quality; a watchmaker talks about precision, not about precisement.
normal.cn: precision 加 -ion 表示性质；表匠说的是 precision，而不是另造一个名词。

normal.en: Precisely at six and precisely because both stress a perfect fit, one of time and one of reason.
normal.cn: precisely at six 与 precisely because 都在强调严丝合缝，一个扣时间，一个扣理由。

normal.en: A one-word Precisely in conversation is the same judgement made aloud and then stopped.
normal.cn: 对话里单独一个 Precisely，就是把同一个判断说出声，然后就此打住。

normal.en: Imprecise is the word with in-, not exact and often slightly vague by accident.
normal.cn: imprecise 是加上 in- 的否定式，意为不精确，常带一点无意间含糊的意味。

abstract.en: Accuracy is subtraction, not addition: the word says so every time it is used.
abstract.cn: 准确是减法而不是加法：这个词每次被使用都在这样说。

abstract.en: A clock and an argument can both be precise, because both can be judged by how well the edges meet.
abstract.cn: 钟表和论证都可以很 precise，因为两者都能用「边角是否对齐」来判断。

abstract.en: When someone answers precisely, they are confirming that no word needs to be moved.
abstract.cn: 有人回答 precisely 时，是在确认这句话里没有一个词需要挪动。

examples.en: The instrument measures the temperature precisely.
examples.cn: 这台仪器能精确测量温度。

examples.en: The power failed precisely at the moment the speech began.
examples.cn: 就在演讲开始的那一刻，电停了。

examples.en: She recorded every reading precisely, down to the last decimal.
examples.cn: 她把每个读数都记到小数点最后一位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞赛斯利」——切得干净利落，一点毛边都不留；precisely 就是精确地。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ caedere（切）→ praecidere（切掉、截短）→ 分词 praecisus → 英语 precise → 加 -ly 成 precisely。同族有 precision、imprecise。

sensesIntro.en: The senses follow one idea: everything extra has been cut away, so a figure is exact, a moment is exactly that moment, an answer is exactly right, and a method leaves no detail loose.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项沿着同一个念头展开：多余的部分都被切掉了，所以数字准确、时刻分毫不差、回答完全正确、做法不放过任何细节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second hand pressed against a mark on the dial, held there without the smallest drift.
core.cn: 核心意象：秒针压在表盘的刻度线上，停在那里，没有一丝偏移。

branches.en: a gauge needle settling on a hairline mark
branches.cn: 表针停在细如发丝的刻度上

branches.en: a switch thrown at the exact second a speech starts
branches.cn: 在演讲开始那一秒被拉下的开关

branches.en: a single word of agreement that ends the discussion
branches.cn: 一个词结束整场讨论

branches.en: a record book filled to the last decimal place
branches.cn: 记到小数点最后一位的记录本

branches.en: a measurement and a method both trimmed clean
branches.cn: 一次测量与一套做法都被修得干净

intro.en: A Latin verb of cutting, a prefix of being in front, and English -ly hold the word together; its family also gives the noun precision and the negated imprecise.
intro.cn: 一个表示切的拉丁动词、一个表示「在前」的前缀，加上英语的 -ly，共同撑起这个词；同族还有名词 precision 与否定式 imprecise。

latinIntro.en: Caedere, praecidere and the participle praecisus are all securely recorded Latin forms, so the family is well documented rather than reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: caedere、praecidere 以及分词 praecisus 都是有可靠记录的拉丁语形式，所以这一族词有据可查，而非重构。

items.meaning: to cut off, to cut short

latinEntries.meaning: to cut off, to cut short

definition_zh: 热切的；渴望的；敏锐的；锋利的；激烈的
definition_en: very eager to do something, or sharp in mind, sense, or edge
core_image: 刀口在光下反出一道细白线，一眼看去就让人缩手
scene: 雪后清早，几个人在门口换鞋，谁都想第一个上坡。 The children are keen to see the snow before it melts.
sceneCN: 这里 keen 是「热切的、渴望的」（第 1 个义项：非常想做某事），句意为孩子们急着想在雪化前去看雪。画面里的物件：门口、雪、换鞋的人。

pos.zh: 形容词：热切的；渴望的；敏锐的；锋利的；激烈的

derivatives.zh: 由 keen 加 -ly 构成，义为「热切地；敏锐地」
由 keen 加 -ness 构成，义为「热心；锐利」

senses.title: Very eager to do something
senses.definition: very much wanting to do something or to have something happen
senses.definitionCN: 非常想做某事或希望某事发生
senses.example: He was keen to start work that same week.
senses.exampleCN: 他迫切想当周就开始工作。
senses.why: The sharp edge of wanting points forward at the thing not yet had.
senses.whyCN: 渴望那道「锋刃」朝前指着还没到手的那个东西。

senses.title: Sharp in mind or sense
senses.definition: quick to notice, understand, or feel
senses.definitionCN: 注意、理解或感受得很快
senses.example: She has a keen ear for small changes in tone.
senses.exampleCN: 她对语调里的细微变化很敏感。
senses.why: A faculty described as keen is one that cuts into detail.
senses.whyCN: 被称作 keen 的能力，是能切进细节的那种能力。

senses.title: Sharp in edge
senses.definition: having a fine, cutting edge
senses.definitionCN: 指刀刃又细又快
senses.example: The knife is keen enough to cut paper.
senses.exampleCN: 这把刀快得能切纸。
senses.why: This is the literal edge from which all the other senses borrow their sharpness.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面的刃口，其他各义的「锐利」都从这里借来。

senses.title: Intense or strong in feeling
senses.definition: strong and intense, as of competition, interest, or wind
senses.definitionCN: 指竞争、兴趣或风等强烈而凌厉
senses.example: Competition for the place was keen.
senses.exampleCN: 这个名额的竞争很激烈。
senses.why: Intensity is pressure concentrated on a narrow point, like an edge.
senses.whyCN: 强度就是集中在一点上的压力，像一条刃。

senses.title: Bitter and cold, of weather
senses.definition: piercingly cold, as of wind
senses.definitionCN: 指风等冷得刺人
senses.example: A keen wind came off the water.
senses.exampleCN: 水面上吹来一阵刺骨的风。
senses.why: A wind that feels sharp is weather described with the edge image.
senses.whyCN: 感觉锋利的风，是用刃的画面去写天气。

senses.title: A wailing lament for the dead
senses.definition: a loud lament for a dead person, chiefly Irish usage
senses.definitionCN: 主要指爱尔兰习俗中为死者发出的哭号
senses.example: The women raised a keen over the body.
senses.exampleCN: 妇女们为遗体唱起挽歌。
senses.why: This noun is a separate borrowing, though the cry is high and piercing like the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是另一次借词，但那种哭声高而尖，与形容词的感觉相通。

intro.en: Keen comes from Old English cene, meaning bold and brave, and only later took on sharpness and eagerness.
intro.cn: keen 来自古英语 cene「勇敢的」，较晚才发展出「锋利、热切」等义。

items.en: cene meant bold, brave, or fierce in battle.
items.cn: cene 意为战斗中勇敢、勇猛。

items.en: Middle English kene widened to sharp, severe, and quick.
items.cn: 中古英语 kene 扩展到尖锐、严厉、敏捷。

items.en: Related Norse forms reinforced the sense of sharpness and edge.
items.cn: 相关的古北欧语形式加强了「锐利」的感觉。

items.en: The eagerness sense settled in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 「热切」义在十九世纪固定下来。

items.en: The noun keen for a lament came from Irish caoineadh.
items.cn: 表示挽歌的名词 keen 来自爱尔兰语 caoineadh。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words that look like keen; the near-meaning group holds adjectival first cousins.
note.cn: 形近组收外形容易与 keen 混的短词；近义组收几个形容词近亲。

entries.definition: To have or hold something.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写只差一个字母，义为「保持；保留」，来源不同。

entries.definition: A small barrel.
A small twist or tight bend.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近，义为「扭结；小弯」，来源不同。

entries.definition: Wanting something very much.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「渴望的」，与第 1 个义项最近。

entries.definition: Having a fine edge or quick mind.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「锋利的；机敏的」。

entries.definition: Very sharp or very strong.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指极为敏锐或强烈。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a brave fighter to a knife and then to a keen student.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从勇敢的战士走到刀刃，再走到热心的学生。

normal.en: Old English cene meant brave, not eager.
normal.cn: 古英语 cene 意为勇敢，而不是热切。

normal.en: Keen on is the preposition for interest, as in keen on music.
normal.cn: 表示兴趣用 keen on，如 keen on music。

normal.en: Keen to do takes the infinitive.
normal.cn: keen to do 后接动词不定式。

normal.en: A keen eye is a sharp eye, not an eager one.
normal.cn: a keen eye 指眼力锐利，不是心急。

normal.en: The Irish keen is a wail over the dead.
normal.cn: 爱尔兰语来源的 keen 是为逝者哭号。

abstract.en: Keen is a blade of attention.
abstract.cn: keen 是注意力磨出的刃口。

abstract.en: Sharp edge, sharp mind, sharp wind: one image, three places.
abstract.cn: 刃利、头脑利、风利：一个比喻用在三处。

abstract.en: The eager and the edged share their keenness.
abstract.cn: 渴望与锋锐共用同一份「利」。

examples.en: She is keen on learning another language.
examples.cn: 她很热衷于学另一门语言。

definition_zh: 系列；连续；丛书；（广播或电视）系列节目
definition_en: a number of similar things coming one after another
core_image: 书架上一排同款书籍，书脊整齐地排成一行
scene: 图书馆新到一批科普读物，馆员逐本上架。 She bought the third volume of the popular science series.
sceneCN: 这里 series 是「丛书；系列」（第 3 个义项：成套出版的同类读物）；句意是她买了这套畅销科普丛书的第三册。

derivatives.zh: series 加 -ize 动词后缀，义为「连载；序列化」

senses.title: Several similar things following one another
senses.definition: many similar events or objects in succession
senses.definitionCN: 相继出现的多个同类事件或物品
senses.example: A series of accidents forced the road to close.
senses.exampleCN: 一连串事故迫使道路关闭。
senses.why: One shelf, one look: the books stand like one word repeated.
senses.whyCN: 一个书架，一个模样：那些书像同一个词的反复出现。

senses.title: A set of broadcasts or episodes
senses.definition: a show released in connected parts
senses.definitionCN: 分集播出的节目
senses.example: The new comedy series starts in May.
senses.exampleCN: 这部新喜剧五月开播。
senses.why: The same look returns every week on screen.
senses.whyCN: 同样的模样每周在屏幕上回归。

senses.title: A set of books published as one group
senses.definition: books issued one by one under one title plan
senses.definitionCN: 按同一规划陆续出版的成套书籍
senses.example: This series explains science for children.
senses.exampleCN: 这套丛书为孩子讲解科学。
senses.why: Each volume repeats the same spine until the set is full.
senses.whyCN: 每一卷都重复着同样的书脊，直到成套。

senses.title: Sports matches played in succession
senses.definition: a group of games between the same teams
senses.definitionCN: 同两队之间连续进行的比赛
senses.example: The teams split the series two all.
senses.exampleCN: 两队以二比二平分系列赛。
senses.why: The shelf becomes a row of match days.
senses.whyCN: 书架变成了一排比赛日。

senses.title: In electrical circuits, one after another
senses.definition: connected so current passes through each part in turn
senses.definitionCN: 电流依次流过各部件的连接方式
senses.example: The bulbs are wired in series.
senses.exampleCN: 这些灯泡是串联的。
senses.why: The row of books becomes a row of bulbs sharing one wire.
senses.whyCN: 书排变成了共用电线的一排灯泡。

intro.en: From Latin series, a row or chain, from serere (to join, link).
intro.cn: 来自拉丁语 series「一列、一串」，源于 serere（连接、串起）。

items.en: A root *ser- means to line up or join, seen in assert.
items.cn: 词根 *ser- 意为「排成一行、连接」，也见于 assert。

items.en: Serere means to bind together; series is the joined row.
items.cn: 拉丁语 serere 意为「串起」；series 就是串成的一列。

items.en: Roman writers used series for chains of causes and rows of books.
items.cn: 罗马作家用 series 指因果链与书列。

items.en: Later scholars kept series for ordered sets in math and logic.
items.cn: 后世学者在数学与逻辑中沿用 series 表示有序集合。

items.en: English adopted series around 1600; broadcasting uses grew in the 1900s.
items.cn: 英语约在 1600 年借入 series；二十世纪又发展出广播义。

note.en: Look-alikes in the seri- family, and near rivals in the succession field.
note.cn: seri- 词族的形近词，以及「接连」义场的近义词。

entries.definition: to work for or deliver

abstract.cn: 看见比赛日一张接一张钉上墙

abstract.cn: 体会一根电线静静串起每只灯泡

examples.cn: 博物馆将举办一系列爵士音乐会。

examples.cn: 她的侦探系列丛书已售出数百万册。

definition_zh: 恢复；修复；归还
definition_en: to bring something back to an earlier or better condition
core_image: 工匠把一件破损的旧物一点点修补回原样
scene: 洪水退去后，村民们一起修复被冲毁的石桥。 After the flood went down, the villagers worked together to restore the damaged stone bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 restore 是「修复」（第 2 个义项：把受损的建筑修回原状）；句意：洪水退去后，村民们一起修复被冲毁的石桥。

derivatives.zh: 恢复；修复
有助于恢复的
修复者

senses.title: Bring back a condition
senses.definition: to make something return to its former condition
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物回到原来的状态
senses.example: The new manager quickly restored calm in the office.
senses.exampleCN: 新经理很快恢复了办公室的平静。
senses.why: The Latin source means to rebuild, so restoring is putting a good state back.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为重建，因此 restore 就是让良好的状态重新回来。

senses.title: Repair something old
senses.definition: to repair an old building, painting or object so that it looks as it did
senses.definitionCN: 修理古老的建筑、画作或物品，使其恢复原貌
senses.example: Experts spent years restoring the ancient temple.
senses.exampleCN: 专家们花了多年时间修复这座古庙。
senses.why: Repairing an old thing is a physical way of giving it back its earlier state.
senses.whyCN: 修复旧物，是以实物的方式让它回到早先的状态。

senses.title: Give something back
senses.definition: to return something that was lost or taken
senses.definitionCN: 把丢失或被拿走的东西交还
senses.example: The police restored the stolen painting to its owner.
senses.exampleCN: 警方把被盗的画作归还给了失主。
senses.why: Returning an object puts it back where it belongs, which is another kind of restoring.
senses.whyCN: 把物品送还原处，是另一种意义上的恢复。

intro.en: Restore comes from Latin restaurare, to rebuild, through Old French restorer.
intro.cn: restore 经古法语 restorer 源自拉丁语 restaurare（重建）。

items.en: Restaurare means to rebuild or renew.
items.cn: restaurare 意为重建或更新。

items.en: The prefix re- adds the idea of again.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 增加「再次」的含义。

items.en: Restorer carries the meaning into French.
items.cn: restorer 把这一含义带入法语。

items.en: English restore covers repair and recovery.
items.cn: 英语 restore 涵盖修理与复原。

items.en: Restore now also means to give something back.
items.cn: 现代英语中 restore 还表示归还。

note.en: Restore is close to words for repairing and bringing back.
note.cn: restore 与表示修理和带回的词相近。

making you feel healthy again
someone who repairs old things

normalIntro.en: Restore is re- plus store: put the good condition back into store again.
normalIntro.cn: restore 是 re- 加 store：把良好的状态重新存回去。

normal.en: Restore order means bring calm back.
normal.cn: restore order 意为把秩序带回来。

normal.en: Restore a building means repair it carefully.
normal.cn: restore a building 意为仔细修好建筑。

normal.en: Restore power means make the lights work again.
normal.cn: restore power 意为让电灯重新亮起。

normal.en: The noun restoration names the whole repair process.
normal.cn: 名词 restoration 指整个修复过程。

normal.en: Compare repair: repair fixes damage, restore also brings back the original look.
normal.cn: 对比 repair：repair 修好损坏，restore 还恢复原貌。

abstract.en: Picture a cracked vase slowly becoming whole.
abstract.cn: 想象一只裂开的瓶子慢慢变得完整。

abstract.en: Imagine a switch bringing a dark street back to light.
abstract.cn: 想象一个开关让黑暗的街道重新亮起。

abstract.en: Think of an old photo cleaned until the faces return.
abstract.cn: 想象一张旧照片被擦净，人脸重新显现。

examples.en: The medicine helped restore her strength.
examples.cn: 这种药帮助她恢复了体力。

examples.en: Workers restored the old theater to its former beauty.
examples.cn: 工人们把老剧院修复到了昔日的美丽模样。

examples.en: He restored the borrowed book to the library shelf.
examples.cn: 他把借来的书放回了图书馆的书架。

sensesIntro.cn: restore 先指恢复状态，再指修复古物，最后指把东西归还原主。

definition_zh: 不幸地；遗憾的是；不巧；可惜
definition_en: in a way that is bad luck or a cause of regret, often used to open a sentence
core_image: 话还没说完，先一声轻轻的叹气
scene: 电话那头安静了一会儿，然后才传来婉拒的答复。 Unfortunately, the tickets were already gone.
sceneCN: 这里 unfortunately 是「遗憾的是」（第 2 个义项：表示惋惜的评注）；句意为可惜票已经卖完了。一声先于说话的叹气，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 副词去掉 -ly 的形容词形式，义为「不幸的」
肯定形式加 -ly 的副词，义为「幸运地」
词族核心名词，义为「运气；财富」
用 mis- 表坏的近义词，义为「不幸；灾祸」

senses.title: By bad luck
senses.definition: by an unlucky turn of events rather than by anyone fault
senses.definitionCN: 由于事态的不巧转折，而非任何人的过错
senses.example: Unfortunately, the rain started just as the ceremony began.
senses.exampleCN: 不巧的是，仪式刚开始就下起了雨。
senses.why: The adverb returns to the oldest sense of fortune as chance and says the chance went wrong.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词回到 fortune 最古老的「机遇」之义，只是说机遇走坏了。

senses.title: Regrettably, used as a comment
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to soften bad or unwelcome news
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，用来软化坏消息或不那么受欢迎的答复
senses.example: Unfortunately, we cannot offer you the position.
senses.exampleCN: 很遗憾，这个职位我们无法录用你。
senses.why: A word of bad chance placed outside the sentence turns into a polite frame for news.
senses.whyCN: 被放到句子外面的「坏运气」，就成了一种通报消息的礼貌包装。

senses.title: At a badly chosen moment
senses.definition: used of something that happens at an awkward time
senses.definitionCN: 形容某事发生在很尴尬的时间点
senses.example: The announcement came unfortunately close to the election.
senses.exampleCN: 这项宣布来得离选举太近，很不凑巧。
senses.why: Timing is part of chance, so a bad hour is a small piece of bad fortune.
senses.whyCN: 时机本是机遇的一部分，因此一个坏时刻就是一小片坏运气。

senses.title: With real loss or hardship
senses.definition: used when the outcome involves genuine harm to someone
senses.definitionCN: 用于结果确实对某人造成伤害的场合
senses.example: Unfortunately, the files had not been saved.
senses.exampleCN: 不幸的是，那些文件没有保存。
senses.why: The mild and the grave uses sit on one scale, and only the context sets the weight.
senses.whyCN: 轻重两种用法在同一条刻度上，只有语境才决定它的分量。

senses.title: In a reply, as a soft no
senses.definition: used in conversation as a gentle way of refusing or correcting
senses.definitionCN: 在对话中委婉地拒绝或纠正他人
senses.example: Unfortunately not, the shop closes at six.
senses.exampleCN: 抱歉不行，那家店六点就关门了。
senses.why: Polite refusals borrow the language of chance so that nobody takes the blame.
senses.whyCN: 委婉的拒绝借用了「运气」的说法，好让谁都不必担责。

intro.en: The adverb is unfortunate plus -ly, with fortune reaching English through French from Latin.
intro.cn: 这个副词是 unfortunate 加 -ly，而 fortune 经法语从拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: Fors meant chance, and Fortuna personified it.
items.cn: fors 意为机遇，Fortuna 则是它的拟人化。

items.en: Fortune named chance and what chance gave, good or bad.
items.cn: fortune 指机遇以及它给予的东西，好坏皆可。

items.en: English adopted fortune, later extending it to wealth.
items.cn: 英语采用 fortune，后来延伸到财富。

items.en: Fortunate and unfortunate were built from the noun in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 十六世纪由这个名词构成 fortunate 与 unfortunate。

items.en: -ly produced the adverb, which settled at the head of sentences.
items.cn: 加 -ly 得到副词，后来固定在句首使用。

note.en: The look-alike group holds fortune forms, and the near-meaning group gathers sentence adverbs of regret.
note.cn: 形近组是 fortune 的各种形式，近义组汇集表示遗憾的句子副词。

normal.cn: un- 加 fortunately：运气不好。

normal.cn: unfortunately not 是口语中常见的委婉拒绝。

normal.en: Fortunately is the buoyant twin used for good outcomes.
normal.cn: fortunately 是它的乐观孪生词，用于好结果。

normal.cn: unfortunately for someone 把坏运气缩到某一个人身上。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised half way before the refusal is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象拒绝还没说出口，一只手先半举起来。

abstract.en: Hear the sigh that comes before the word on the phone.
abstract.cn: 听电话里那个词之前的一声叹气。

abstract.en: See a weather app open with rain on every day of the trip.
abstract.cn: 看旅行那几天天气预报上全是雨。

examples.en: Unfortunately, the last train had already left when we arrived.
examples.cn: 可惜的是，我们到的时候末班车已经开走了。

examples.en: Unfortunately for him, the only seat was in the sun.
examples.cn: 对他来说不幸的是，唯一的座位在太阳底下。

definition_en: to choose someone by voting, to decide to do something, or describing someone chosen but not yet in office
core_image: 一只只手举起，票箱被封上，名字被念出来
scene: 会场里一只手接一只手举起，票数很快过半。 The members elected a new chair by a clear majority.
sceneCN: 这里 elect 是「选举」（第 1 个义项：通过投票选出某人）；句意是成员以明显多数选出了新主席。

pos.zh: 动词：选举；推选；选择做（某事）
形容词：当选而尚未就职的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「选举」

senses.title: To choose by voting
senses.definition: to choose a person for an office or position by voting
senses.definitionCN: 通过投票为某个职位选出某人
senses.example: The members elected a new chair by a clear majority.
senses.exampleCN: 成员以明显多数选出了新主席。
senses.why: Elect is Latin eligere, e- out plus legere to pick: the choice is picked out and then made public.
senses.whyCN: elect 是拉丁语 eligere，由 e-（出）加 legere（挑选）构成：这个选择被挑出来，然后公开。

senses.title: To decide to do something
senses.definition: to choose to do something, especially in formal or official language
senses.definitionCN: 选择去做某事，尤用于正式或官方语境
senses.example: The company elected to remain silent.
senses.exampleCN: 公司选择保持沉默。
senses.why: The same picking happens inside one head instead of a hall, so elect can mean simply to choose.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「挑选」发生在一个脑袋里而不是大厅里，所以 elect 也能只表示「选择」。

senses.title: Chosen but not yet in office
senses.definition: used after a title for someone who has been elected but has not yet taken up the post
senses.definitionCN: 用在头衔之后，指已经当选但尚未上任的人
senses.example: The president elect will be sworn in in January.
senses.exampleCN: 当选总统将于一月宣誓就职。
senses.why: The pick has been made but the office is still empty, so the adjective marks that gap in time.
senses.whyCN: 人选已经挑定，而职位还空着，于是这个形容词标记出这段时间空隙。

intro.en: Elect comes from Latin eligere, to pick out, from e- out plus legere, to choose or read, and reached English through the participle electus.
intro.cn: elect 来自拉丁语 eligere（挑出），由 e-（出）加 legere（挑选、读）构成，经分词 electus 进入英语。

items.en: Legere meant to gather, pick or read, and it also gave lecture and legend.
items.cn: legere 意为「收集、挑选、读」，也生出 lecture 与 legend。

items.en: E- out plus legere formed eligere, to pick out from among others.
items.cn: e-（出）加 legere 构成 eligere，意为「从众人中挑出来」。

items.en: The participle electus meant picked out, hence chosen.
items.cn: 分词 electus 意为「被挑出的」，因此是「被选中的」。

items.en: The noun named the act of picking out, the source of election.
items.cn: 名词指「挑选」这一动作，是 election 的来源。

items.en: English borrowed the verb for choosing a person to an office.
items.cn: 英语借入这个动词，指为某个职位选出人选。

items.en: The bare verb also took the milder sense of deciding, and the adjective use followed.
items.cn: 光杆动词又带上「决定」的温和义，形容词用法随后出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the election family; the near-meaning group separates choose, vote and appoint.
note.cn: 形近组收 election 词族；近义组区分 choose、vote 与 appoint。

entries.definition: A person who has the right to vote in an election.

entries.definition: To record a formal choice; it names the act inside an election.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「投票」，指选举中的那个动作。

entries.definition: To give someone a job or post by decision rather than by vote.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「任命」，由决定而非投票产生。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a hall of raised hands, then narrow to one private decision and one gap before taking office.

abstract.cn: 同一种挑选可以是公开的或私下的，也可以让一个名字单独立着。

definition_zh: 核心；果核；要点
definition_en: the central or most important part of something

scene: 老师把苹果横着切开，让学生看中间那一圈小小的籽。 The core of an apple holds its seeds in a small room.
sceneCN: 这里 core 指「果核」（第 2 个义项：果实中央装种子的部分）；句意是苹果的果核像一间小屋，装着它的种子。

derivatives.zh: 去核器

senses.title: The central part
senses.definition: the central or most important part of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物最中心或最重要的部分
senses.example: The core of the team is its two oldest players.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍的核心是两位最年长的球员。
senses.why: Every circle needs a middle before it can have an edge.
senses.whyCN: 每个圆都要先有中心，才能有边缘。

senses.title: The seed chamber of fruit
senses.definition: the hard central part of an apple or pear that holds the seeds
senses.definitionCN: 苹果或梨中间装着种子的硬心
senses.example: Cut the apple and take out the core.
senses.exampleCN: 把苹果切开，取出果核。
senses.why: The fruit builds a small room for its seeds and calls it a core.
senses.whyCN: 果实为种子盖了一间小屋，管它叫果核。

senses.title: The central meaning
senses.definition: the central idea or meaning of an argument or a text
senses.definitionCN: 论点或文章最中心的观点或意思
senses.example: The core of her argument is simple.
senses.exampleCN: 她论点的要点很简单。
senses.why: Strip away the leaves of words and a few hard seeds remain.

items.en: The stem cord- carried the same sense into compounds.

items.en: English core first named the inner part of fruit.

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a fruit cut open, then move to a team and to the heart of an argument.

normal.en: Cor is Latin for heart, so the core is the heart of anything.
normal.cn: cor 在拉丁语里是心，所以 core 就是任何事物的心。

normal.en: An apple keeps its seeds in the core, as a house keeps its family in one room.
normal.cn: 苹果把种子留在果核里，就像房子把家人留在一间屋里。

normal.en: Cut away everything soft and the core still stands.
normal.cn: 把柔软的部分都切掉，果核还立在那里。

normal.en: A team has a core: the few people the others lean on.
normal.cn: 一支队伍有核心，就是其他人都依靠的那几个人。

normal.en: If you forget the sense, picture the hard middle you never eat.
normal.cn: 如果忘了意思，就想想那个你从不吃的硬心。

abstract.en: Picture a hard stone at the centre of a peach.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗硬核躺在桃子正中。

abstract.en: Picture a wheel whose hub holds every spoke.
abstract.cn: 想象一个轮子，轮毂把所有辐条收拢在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence with all its modifiers peeled away.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话被剥去所有修饰，只剩主干。

examples.en: The core of the city is its old square.

branches.en: From fruit to thought, the core is the part that must stay.

definition_zh: 聚集；收集；推断；增加
definition_en: to come together, to collect things, to understand from evidence, or to increase gradually
core_image: 广场上的人们从四面聚拢到一起
scene: 人群在广场上聚集起来。 A crowd gathered in the square.
sceneCN: 这里 gather 是「聚集」（第 1 个义项）；句意：人群在广场上聚集起来。

derivatives.zh: 聚会；集会
采集者

senses.title: Come together
senses.definition: to come together in one place
senses.definitionCN: 来到同一个地方聚在一起
senses.example: A crowd gathered in the square.
senses.exampleCN: 人群在广场上聚集起来。
senses.why: This is the central sense of people meeting.
senses.whyCN: 这是人们会合的核心义项。

senses.title: Collect things
senses.definition: to bring things together from different places
senses.definitionCN: 从不同地方把东西收拢到一起
senses.example: They gathered wood for the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 他们捡来木柴生火。
senses.why: The word extends from people to objects.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从人扩展到物品。

senses.title: Understand from clues
senses.definition: to understand something from the information available
senses.definitionCN: 根据已有信息理解某事
senses.example: I gather that the meeting was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 我推断会议取消了。
senses.why: Pieces of evidence are mentally collected.
senses.whyCN: 证据的碎片在头脑中被收拢起来。

senses.title: Increase gradually
senses.definition: to gradually gain speed, strength, or force
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐获得速度、力量或势头
senses.example: The train gathered speed down the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 火车下山时越来越快。
senses.why: Force is pictured as something being collected.
senses.whyCN: 力量被想象成不断被收集起来的东西。

intro.en: Gather is an Old English verb for bringing things into one place.
intro.cn: gather 是古英语动词，意为把东西聚到一处。

items.en: Gaderian meant to bring together or unite.
items.cn: gaderian 意为聚拢或联合。

items.en: Related forms in other Germanic languages shared the sense.
items.cn: 其他日耳曼语中的相关形式也有同样的意思。

items.en: The verb took the form gaderen and later gather.
items.cn: 这个动词先后写作 gaderen 和 gather。

items.en: It widened to collecting crops, facts, and evidence.
items.cn: 词义扩展到收割庄稼、收集事实和证据。

items.en: It also came to mean drawing a conclusion.
items.cn: 它也发展为得出结论的意思。

note.en: Gather is compared with look-alike words and other verbs of bringing together.
note.cn: 把 gather 与形近词以及其他表示聚拢的动词作比较。

entries.definition: a band worn around the leg
a channel at the edge of a road
to shine with small bright flashes
to bring things together
to bring people or parts together
to increase by adding more and more

normalIntro.en: To gather is to make many separate things into one group.
normalIntro.cn: gather 就是把许多分散的东西变成一个整体。

normal.en: A crowd gathered in the square.
normal.cn: 人群在广场上聚集起来。

normal.en: They gathered wood for the fire.
normal.cn: 他们捡来木柴生火。

normal.en: I gather that the meeting was cancelled.
normal.cn: 我推断会议取消了。

normal.en: The train gathered speed down the hill.
normal.cn: 火车下山时越来越快。

normal.en: We gathered around the small table.
normal.cn: 我们围拢在小桌旁。

abstract.en: Attention gathers what the eye alone would scatter.
abstract.cn: 注意力把眼睛本会散落的东西聚拢起来。

abstract.en: A community begins when people gather for no practical reason.
abstract.cn: 人们为没有实际目的的事情聚在一起时，社群就开始了。

abstract.en: Small facts gather into understanding.
abstract.cn: 细小的事实汇聚成理解。

examples.cn: 人群在广场上聚集起来。

examples.en: I gather that the meeting was cancelled.
examples.cn: 我推断会议取消了。

dict_mnemonic.text: gather 与 together 同源，都含「聚到一起」的意思；gather speed 是「加速」，gather information 是「收集信息」。

root: 古英语 gaderian（聚拢、联合），与 together 同源，核心义「把分散之物聚到一处」。

sensesIntro.en: Gather means to come together, to collect, to infer, or to increase gradually.
sensesIntro.cn: gather 意为聚到一起、收集、推断，或逐渐增加。

core.en: Separate parts brought into one place.
core.cn: 把分散的部分聚到一处。

branches.en: People arrive until they form a crowd.
branches.cn: 人们陆续到来，直到围成一群。

branches.en: Hands pick up wood and crops.
branches.cn: 双手捡起木柴和庄稼。

branches.en: Clues are joined into a conclusion.
branches.cn: 线索被拼接成结论。

branches.en: Speed builds as a train rolls downhill.
branches.cn: 火车下坡时速度不断累积。

branches.en: People and things are both brought together.
branches.cn: 人与物都会被聚拢到一起。

intro.en: Gather builds words for meetings and for people who collect.
intro.cn: gather 构成表示聚会和采集者的词。

latinIntro.en: The verb is Germanic in origin and has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 这个动词源于日耳曼语，没有拉丁语词根。

items.exampleCN: 人们每天傍晚在这里聚集。

items.example: She gathers herbs in the morning.
It was a quiet family gathering.
items.exampleCN: 那是一次安静的家庭聚会。

items.example: The gatherer filled a basket with berries.
items.exampleCN: 采集者用浆果装满了篮子。

items.meaning: to come close in a group
items.example: The children gathered around the fire.
The bus gathered speed on the straight road.
items.exampleCN: 公交车在直路上加快了速度。

items.example: The police gathered evidence for weeks.
items.exampleCN: 警方收集证据达数周之久。

definition_zh: 电的；用电的；电动的；令人激动的
definition_en: relating to electricity itself, working by electricity, or filled with tense excitement
core_image: 指尖刚碰到门把手，啪地跳出一小簇火花
scene: 雨夜里水壶的开关一跳，壶身很快就响了。 The electric kettle switched itself off with a click.
sceneCN: 这里 electric 是「用电的」（第 2 个义项：靠电力工作的器具）；句意是那只电水壶咔一声自动断电。

pos.zh: 形容词：电的；用电的；电动的；令人激动的

senses.title: Of electricity itself
senses.definition: relating to electricity as a physical force, as in current, charge or field
senses.definitionCN: 指作为物理力量的电，如电流、电荷、电场
senses.example: The electric charge built up on the dry cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 干燥的布上积聚起了电荷。
senses.why: Electric comes from amber, which when rubbed attracts things; the word first named that force itself.
senses.whyCN: electric 来自琥珀，摩擦后会吸东西；这个词最初指的就是那股力量本身。

senses.title: Working by electricity
senses.definition: of a machine or device, driven by electricity rather than by fuel or by hand
senses.definitionCN: 指机器或设备，由电力而非燃料或人力驱动
senses.example: The electric kettle switched itself off with a click.
senses.exampleCN: 那只电水壶咔一声自动断电。
senses.why: Once the force had a name, anything running on it was simply described with the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这股力量一旦有了名字，任何靠它运转的东西就用同一个形容词来描述。

senses.title: Tense with excitement
senses.definition: filled with a tense, exciting feeling, as if a current were running through it
senses.definitionCN: 充满紧张兴奋的感觉，仿佛有电流穿过
senses.example: The hall went electric when the band walked on.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队一上台，整个大厅就沸腾了。
senses.why: A shock runs through the body, so a crowd in suspense is described as carrying the same current.
senses.whyCN: 电击会穿过身体，于是屏息的人群也被说成带着同一股电流。

intro.en: Electric was coined in the seventeenth century from Latin electrum, amber, from Greek elektron, because rubbed amber attracts light objects.
intro.cn: electric 是十七世纪由拉丁语 electrum（琥珀）造出，源自希腊语 elektron，因为摩擦过的琥珀会吸起轻物。

items.en: Elektron meant amber, the fossil resin that first showed the effect.
items.cn: elektron 意为「琥珀」，就是最先显现这种效应的树脂化石。

items.en: Latin kept electrum for amber and for a pale gold alloy.
items.cn: 拉丁语用 electrum 指琥珀，也指一种淡金色的合金。

items.en: Seventeenth-century scientists formed electricus for the force shown by rubbed amber.
items.cn: 十七世纪科学家造出 electricus，指摩擦琥珀所显现的那股力。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective and applied it first to bodies that attract.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，最初用于会吸引轻物的物体。

items.en: Industry widened it to machines, and writers stretched it to excitement.
items.cn: 工业把它扩展到机器，作家又把它拉向情绪上的激动。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the electricity family; the near-meaning group separates electrical, electronic and electrifying.
note.cn: 形近组收 electricity 词族；近义组区分 electrical、electronic 与 electrifying。

entries.definition: Relating to electricity as a system or field of engineering, rather than to one device.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「与电有关的、电气的」，指系统或工程，而非单个器具。

entries.definition: The energy carried by moving charges, or the supply of it.
A person who installs and repairs electrical wiring.
To charge with electricity, or to thrill suddenly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使带电；使震惊」。

entries.definition: Working by controlling tiny charged particles in circuits, as computers do.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「电子的」，靠控制电路中的带电微粒工作。

entries.definition: Extremely exciting; the feeling sense pushed to its strongest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「极其震撼的」，把情绪义推到最强。

entries.definition: Driven by a stated source, as in battery-powered.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「以……为动力的」，需说明动力来源。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with amber and a spark, then run the same current through kettles and through a crowd.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从琥珀与火花出发，再让同一股电流通过水壶与人群。

normal.en: Electric comes from amber: rub it and it pulls threads toward it.
normal.cn: electric 来自琥珀：摩擦之后它会把细线吸过来。

normal.en: Electric names the force; electrical names the system built around it.
normal.cn: electric 指那股力本身；electrical 指围绕它建立的系统。

normal.en: An electric kettle has a plug; an electrical fault has a cause.
normal.cn: electric kettle 有插头；electrical fault 有原因。

normal.en: A hall can go electric without a single wire.
normal.cn: 大厅可以一根电线也没有却「带电」。

normal.en: Electronic is one step further: not just current, but circuits controlling it.
normal.cn: electronic 再进一步：不只是电流，而是控制电流的电路。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip an inch from a door handle, a spark about to jump.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖离门把手一寸，火花就要跳过去。

abstract.en: The same jump can power a kettle or run through a waiting audience.
abstract.cn: 同一次跳跃可以带动水壶，也可以穿过等待的观众。

abstract.en: Electric is energy looking for somewhere to go.
abstract.cn: electric 就是一股急着找去处的能力。

examples.en: The hall went electric when the band walked on.

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of electric: the physical force itself, devices driven by it, and a mood charged like a current.
sensesIntro.cn: electric 的三个义项：电这股物理力量本身、靠它驱动的器具，以及像电流一样紧绷的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spark jumping from a fingertip to a door handle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一簇火花从指尖跳到门把手上。

branches.en: THE FORCE: current, charge and field as physics names them.
branches.cn: 力量线：物理学所说的电流、电荷与电场。

branches.en: THE DEVICE: a kettle or car that runs on that force.
branches.cn: 器具线：靠这股力运转的水壶或汽车。

branches.en: THE MOOD: a crowd charged like a wire.
branches.cn: 情绪线：人群像导线一样带电。

branches.en: THE SUPPLY: the force and the things it drives are one circuit.
branches.cn: 供给线：力量与它驱动的东西是同一条回路。

branches.en: THE SWITCH: a device turns on, and so does a room.
branches.cn: 开关线：器具被打开，房间也被打开。

intro.en: Electric is a scientific coinage on Greek amber; English adds -ity, -al, -ian, -fy and -onic.
intro.cn: electric 是建立在希腊语「琥珀」上的科学造词；英语再加 -ity、-al、-ian、-fy 与 -onic。

latinIntro.en: Greek elektron and Latin electrum are recorded; electricus is a modern scientific formation, not an ancient word.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 elektron 与拉丁语 electrum 均有记录；electricus 是近代科学造词，不是古语。
