definition_zh: 推荐；建议；使显得可取；托付
definition_en: to praise something as worth choosing; to advise a course of action; to make something attractive; to entrust formally
core_image: 店员把一本书递到顾客手里，说值得一读
scene: 书店里，店员从架上抽出一本小说递到顾客手里。 Librarians often recommend books to new readers.
sceneCN: 这里 recommend 是「推荐」（第 1 个义项：称赞某物值得选择）；句意为图书管理员常向新读者推荐书籍。画面里可留意：递到手里的书、架上的书脊。

pos.zh: 推荐；建议；使显得可取；托付

derivatives.zh: 推荐；建议
值得推荐的
推荐的

senses.title: To praise as worth choosing
senses.definition: to speak in favour of something and suggest that others choose it
senses.definitionCN: 称赞某物并建议他人选择它
senses.example: Librarians often recommend books to new readers.
senses.exampleCN: 图书管理员常向新读者推荐书籍。
senses.why: Commendare meant to praise and entrust, and re- strengthened the praise, so the word pictures praise offered for a choice.
senses.whyCN: commendare 意为称赞与托付，re- 加强了称赞，因此这个词描绘为供人选择而给出的赞美。

senses.title: To advise a course of action
senses.definition: to tell someone what you think they should do
senses.definitionCN: 告诉某人你认为他应当怎么做
senses.example: Doctors recommend regular exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 医生建议经常锻炼。
senses.why: Praise and advice are close: what is worth choosing is also what one should do.
senses.whyCN: 称赞与建议很接近：值得选择的东西，也正是应当去做的事。

senses.title: To make something attractive
senses.definition: to give a place or a plan qualities that invite approval
senses.definitionCN: 赋予某地或某方案令人赞许的品质
senses.example: The quiet garden recommends the house to buyers.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的花园让这所房子更讨买家喜欢。
senses.why: When a place or a plan makes itself pleasing, it is as if it praised itself, and the verb covers that self-praise.
senses.whyCN: 当某地或某方案显得讨人喜欢，它就像在自我称赞，这个动词正涵盖这种自我推荐。

senses.title: To entrust formally
senses.definition: to hand a person or a task into someone's care with confidence
senses.definitionCN: 放心地把人或任务交给他人照管
senses.example: She recommended her children to her sister's care.
senses.exampleCN: 她把孩子托付给姐姐照看。
senses.why: The Latin root also carried the sense of entrusting, because praising someone is a way of handing a task to them.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根也带「托付」义，因为称赞某人，正是把任务交给他的方式。

intro.en: Recommend joins praise to trust: the Latin verb meant both to commend and to entrust, and English kept both directions.
intro.cn: recommend 把称赞与信任连在一起：拉丁动词既指称赞也指托付，英语保留了这两个方向。

items.en: Mandare meant to hand over or command, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: mandare 意为交出或命令，是整个词族的词根。

items.en: Commendare joined com- with mandare and meant to entrust or praise.
items.cn: commendare 由 com- 与 mandare 组成，意为托付或称赞。

items.en: Recommendare strengthened the praise with re- and meant to recommend.
items.cn: recommendare 用 re- 加强称赞，意为推荐。

items.en: French recommander carried the word into English with both senses.
items.cn: 法语 recommander 把称赞与托付两义一起带入英语。

items.en: Modern English added the sense of a place or plan that makes itself attractive.
items.cn: 现代英语又加入了「某地或方案自我推荐」的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs built on the same Latin root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of advising and endorsing.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词根上的动词；近义组收表建议与支持的动词。

entries.definition: To praise formally.
To order with authority.
To ask for forcefully.
To put forward an idea.
To tell someone what is wise.
To put forward a plan.
To declare public support.

normalIntro.en: The word is a second praising: re- adds strength to commend, and praise becomes a suggestion.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「再一次称赞」：re- 为 commend 加强语气，称赞于是变成建议。

normal.en: Re plus commend: praise something twice, and you recommend it.
normal.cn: re 加 commend：把某物称赞两次，就是推荐它。

normal.en: Recommend doing is the pattern; recommend to do is not standard.
normal.cn: recommend doing 是固定结构，recommend to do 不合标准。

normal.en: Highly recommended means many people praise it.
normal.cn: highly recommended 意为很多人称赞它。

normal.en: A doctor recommends a habit; a friend recommends a film.
normal.cn: 医生建议一种习惯，朋友推荐一部电影。

normal.en: Keep the double m: re + commend gives recommend.
normal.cn: 注意双写 m：re 加 commend 构成 recommend。

abstract.en: To recommend is to lend your own judgment to another person.
abstract.cn: 推荐，就是把自己的判断借给别人。

abstract.en: A recommendation is a small promise that the other person will not regret it.
abstract.cn: 推荐是一个小小的承诺：对方不会后悔。

abstract.en: What we recommend reveals what we value more than what we say.
abstract.cn: 我们推荐什么，比我们说什么更能暴露我们的价值。

examples.en: Librarians often recommend books to new readers.
examples.cn: 图书管理员常向新读者推荐书籍。

examples.en: Doctors recommend regular exercise.
examples.cn: 医生建议经常锻炼。

examples.en: The quiet garden recommends the house to buyers.
examples.cn: 安静的花园让这所房子更讨买家喜欢。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）加 commend（称赞）：一再称赞，就是推荐；把值得的东西说给别人听，也就是建议。

root: 拉丁 mandare（托付）→ commendare（称赞、托付）→ recommendare（推荐）→ 法语 recommander → 英语 recommend；同族有 recommendation。

sensesIntro.en: The core is praise offered to guide a choice; the senses move from praising a thing to advising an act, to self-praise, and to formal entrusting.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「为引导选择而给出的称赞」；义项从称赞某物，到建议行动，到自我推荐，再到正式托付。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a book taken from a shelf and placed in another person's hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：从架上抽出一本书，放进另一个人手里。

branches.en: a book handed across a counter
branches.cn: 从柜台递过来的一本书

branches.en: a doctor naming a habit
branches.cn: 医生说出一种习惯

branches.en: a garden that sells itself
branches.cn: 一座自我推销的花园

branches.en: children placed in a sister's care
branches.cn: 孩子被托付给姐姐照看

branches.en: praise and advice in one act
branches.cn: 称赞与建议合为一个动作

intro.en: The family is built on a Latin verb of handing over, and praise grows out of the act of entrusting.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语表「交出」的动词上，称赞从托付这一行为中生长出来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is mandare, to hand over; com- and re- shape it into commend and recommend.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 mandare（交出）；com- 与 re- 把它塑造成 commend 与 recommend。

definition_zh: 货币；通货；流传，通行
definition_en: the money a country uses, or the state of being widely used and believed
core_image: 柜台上摊开几张颜色各异的纸币，图案各不相同
scene: 换汇窗口前，一叠不同颜色的纸币被推到玻璃下面。 She changed her currency before the flight.
sceneCN: 这里 currency 指「货币」（第 1 个义项：一国使用的钱）；句意是她在登机前兑换了货币。

derivatives.zh: 现行的；流通的
目前；当前
货币危机

senses.title: National money
senses.definition: the system of money that a country uses
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家所使用的货币制度
senses.example: The euro is the currency of many countries.
senses.exampleCN: 欧元是许多国家的货币。
senses.why: A country prints its own trust and asks others to accept it.
senses.whyCN: 一个国家印出自己的信用，再请别人接受它。

senses.title: Notes and coins
senses.definition: coins and paper notes used as a medium of exchange
senses.definitionCN: 用作交换媒介的硬币与纸币
senses.example: Foreign currency can be changed at the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 外币可以在那个柜台兑换。
senses.why: Value must take a form you can hand to another person.
senses.whyCN: 价值总得变成一种能递到别人手里的东西。

senses.title: Wide acceptance
senses.definition: the state of being widely used, repeated, or believed
senses.definitionCN: 被广泛使用、传述或相信的状态
senses.example: The rumour gained currency within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 那个传言一周之内就传开了。
senses.why: An idea becomes solid once many mouths carry it.
senses.whyCN: 一个想法被许多张嘴带着走，就变得实在了。

intro.en: Currency comes from Latin currere, to run, through the English word current and the suffix -cy.
intro.cn: currency 源自拉丁语 currere（跑、流动），经英语 current 加后缀 -cy 构成。

items.en: Currere meant to run, as water runs in a channel.
items.cn: currere 意为跑，就像水在河道里流。

items.en: Currens described what is running or flowing.
items.cn: currens 形容正在跑、正在流的东西。

items.en: Current first named the running flow of a river.
items.cn: current 最初指河水奔流。

items.en: Currency named the state of being in use or accepted.
items.cn: currency 指被使用、被接受的状态。

items.en: The word settled on the money that passes from hand to hand.
items.cn: 这个词最终落在人与人之间传递的钱上。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the curr- stem, and the meaning group names what people pay with.
note.cn: 形近组共享 curr- 词干，近义组列出人们用来付钱的东西。

entries.definition: happening or flowing now
entries.definitionCN: 现在正在发生或流动的

entries.definition: a small dried grape used in baking
at the present time
coins and notes used to buy things
entries.definitionCN: 用来买东西的硬币和纸币

entries.definition: money in notes and coins, not in a bank
something offered as a means of payment
entries.definitionCN: 作为支付手段提供的东西

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with paper money leaving a hand and end with a rumour that will not stop travelling.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一张离开手的纸币开始，落到一个停不下来的传言。

normal.en: Currency is value that keeps running between hands.
normal.cn: 货币就是在人与人之间不停跑动的价值。

normal.en: A note is only paper until a country says otherwise.
normal.cn: 纸币本来只是纸，直到国家开口赋予它意义。

normal.en: The same word covers money and rumour, because both circulate.
normal.cn: 同一个词既指钱又指传言，因为两者都在流通。

normal.en: When a saying gains currency, it starts to be spent like coins.
normal.cn: 一句话开始流行，就像硬币一样被花出去。

normal.en: Foreign currency is someone else's printed trust.
normal.cn: 外币，是别人印出来的信用。

abstract.en: Picture a banknote moving from one warm hand to another.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸币从一只温热的手传到另一只。

abstract.en: Picture coins crossing a border in a small cloth bag.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币装在小布袋里越过边境。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence repeated in every kitchen until it sounds true.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话在每个厨房里被重复，直到听起来像真的。

examples.en: The local currency is the yuan.
examples.cn: 当地货币是元。

examples.en: Old sayings can gain currency again.
examples.cn: 老话也能重新流行起来。

examples.en: She kept some foreign currency for the trip.
examples.cn: 她为这次旅行留了一些外币。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 currency 记成「正在跑的钱」：curr 是跑，-ency 是状态，钱在人手之间跑来跑去，就是货币。

root: 源自拉丁语 currere（跑、流动），经古法语与英语 current 加后缀 -cy 构成；本义是「流动之物」，先指河水，后指流通中的钱，再指流传的说法。

sensesIntro.en: From the money a nation prints, to the notes in your hand, to an idea that circulates.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一国印出的钱，到手里的一张纸币，再到一个四处流传的想法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: paper money passing from one hand to the next.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张纸币从一只手传到另一只手。

branches.en: A state declares what counts as money inside its borders.
branches.cn: 国家宣布在它的边界内什么算钱。

branches.en: Notes and coins are the physical form that value takes.
branches.cn: 纸币和硬币，是价值采取的具体形状。

branches.en: An idea that everyone repeats is said to have currency.
branches.cn: 人人都在重复的想法，就被说成「通行」。

branches.en: The money of a country and the notes in your pocket are one system.
branches.cn: 一国的货币和口袋里的纸币，是同一套东西。

branches.en: What circulates is trusted, whether it is a note or a rumour.
branches.cn: 凡是流通的都被信任，不管是纸币还是传言。

intro.en: Currency sits in the curr- family, where the idea of running grows into money and into words on everyone's lips.
intro.cn: currency 属于 curr- 这一族，「跑」的意思长成了钱，也长成了人人嘴边的话。

latinIntro.en: The Latin currere, to run, is the root under current, currency, and recur.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 currere（跑）是 current、currency 与 recur 共同的根。

items.example: The currency fell against the dollar.
items.exampleCN: 这种货币对美元贬值了。

items.example: The current is strong near the rocks.

items.meaning: a bank account for daily use
a place or act of changing money
items.example: The currency exchange opens at nine.

items.exampleCN: 这个港口赚到了硬通货。

items.meaning: a sudden loss of trust in money
items.example: The currency crisis emptied the shops.
items.exampleCN: 货币危机让商店都空了。

items.meaning: a hidden flow beneath the surface
items.example: An undercurrent of anger ran through the room.
items.exampleCN: 房间里流动着一股暗藏的怒气。

items.example: Two concurrent meetings split the staff.
items.exampleCN: 两个同时召开的会议把员工分成了两半。

items.example: The pain may recur in winter.
items.exampleCN: 这种疼痛冬天可能再犯。

definition_zh: 硬的；僵硬的；不易弯的；生硬的；拘谨的；激烈的；（使）僵硬；（价格等）过高
definition_en: firm and hard to bend, or not moving easily because of cold or injury; also unnaturally formal
core_image: 冻在窗框上的抹布——掰都掰不动
scene: 清晨出门取报，寒气让门把手冰手。 My fingers went stiff with cold while I waited outside the shop.
sceneCN: 这里 stiff 是形容词「僵直的」（第 1 个义项：受冷或受伤后不易活动）；句意为我在店外等的时候手指冻僵了。

pos.zh: 形容词：硬的；僵硬的；生硬的；激烈的
动词：使僵硬；（口语）诈取；不给小费

collocations.zh: 在这笔交易上被坑（口语）

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「僵硬地；生硬地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「僵硬；硬度；生硬」
由本词加动词后缀构成，义为「使变硬；变硬」
由本词加动词后缀加副词构成，义为「变僵硬」

senses.title: Firm and not easy to bend
senses.definition: firm and rigid so that bending is difficult
senses.definitionCN: 坚硬而有刚性，不易弯曲
senses.example: New leather shoes are stiff until you wear them in.
senses.exampleCN: 新皮鞋很硬，穿几天才变软。
senses.why: The frozen cloth on the window frame: it keeps its shape and resists your hand.
senses.whyCN: 冻在窗框上的抹布：保持形状、抗拒手劲，即硬挺。

senses.title: Not able to move easily, from cold or injury
senses.definition: painful and difficult to move, as after exercise, injury, or cold
senses.definitionCN: 因运动、受伤或寒冷而疼痛难动
senses.example: He felt stiff after sleeping on the hard floor.
senses.exampleCN: 在硬地板上睡了一夜，他觉得浑身发僵。
senses.why: The same resistance, now living inside the body's joints.
senses.whyCN: 同样的抗拒感，只是移进了身体的关节里。

senses.title: Not natural or relaxed; too formal
senses.definition: unnaturally formal or awkward in manner
senses.definitionCN: 举止不自然、过于正式而显得生硬
senses.example: She gave a stiff smile and turned away.
senses.exampleCN: 她僵硬地笑了笑，转身走开。
senses.why: A face that cannot bend into an easy smile.
senses.whyCN: 一张弯不出自然笑容的脸，即拘谨生硬。

senses.title: Intense and demanding; severe
senses.definition: strong, harsh, or hard to beat, as in stiff competition or a stiff penalty
senses.definitionCN: 强烈、严苛或难以击败的，如激烈竞争、严厉处罚
senses.example: The café faces stiff competition from the chain next door.
senses.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆面临隔壁连锁店的激烈竞争。
senses.why: A wind so hard to bend against it nearly stops you walking.
senses.whyCN: 顶得人寸步难行的硬风，即严酷激烈。

senses.title: Very strong, as a drink or a fine
senses.definition: strong in effect, as alcohol with much spirit, or a price on the high side
senses.definitionCN: 效用强烈，如酒精含量高的酒，或偏高的价格
senses.example: That was a stiff drink—half of it was whiskey.
senses.exampleCN: 那杯酒真烈——一半都是威士忌。
senses.why: The blow that does not bend you but knocks you flat.
senses.whyCN: 一口下去不打弯、直接把人放倒的冲击力。

intro.en: Stiff is an Old English word for rigid, from a Germanic root of being rigid or firm.
intro.cn: stiff 源自古英语，指坚硬僵直，一般认为出自日耳曼语「刚硬」词根。

items.en: A reconstructed root *stif- is thought to mean rigid or inflexible.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *stif- 意为僵硬、不弯。

items.en: Stif meant rigid and firm, of bodies, boards, and punishments alike.
items.cn: 古英语 stif 指坚硬僵直，既形容肢体也形容木板与刑罚。

items.en: Stif kept the rigid sense and stretched to harsh wind, hard duties, and strong drink.
items.cn: 中古英语 stiff 沿用僵硬义，并延伸到烈风、严苛差事与烈酒。

items.en: The formal-manner sense grew: a stiff bow, a stiff greeting.
items.cn: 生硬拘谨义发展起来：僵硬的鞠躬、刻板的寒暄。

items.en: Slang added stiff for a corpse and stiffed for cheating, while stiffen and stiffness formed.
items.cn: 俚语又添 stiff 指尸体、stiffed 指坑骗，并派生出 stiffen 与 stiffness。

note.en: Stiff looks like the unrelated stick, and sits near hardness words of different roots.
note.cn: stiff 拼写上与不相关的 stick 相近，义场靠近词源不同的坚硬词。

entries.definition: a thin piece of wood, or to become fixed to something
entries.definitionCN: 棍；粘住；与 stiff 只差一个字母，词源不同

entries.definition: not moving; continuing until now
entries.definitionCN: 静止的；仍然；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: the people working in an organization, or a long stick
entries.definitionCN: 员工；手杖；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: stiff and not able to bend or change
entries.definitionCN: 刚性的；死板的，较正式，兼指规则不容变通

entries.definition: solid and strongly fixed, not soft
entries.definitionCN: 坚固的；结实的，强调支撑力

entries.definition: soft and lacking firmness
entries.definitionCN: 软塌的；无力的，与僵硬相反

entries.definition: severe and unkind, as punishment or criticism
entries.definitionCN: 严酷的；苛刻的，对应 stiff 的严厉义

normalIntro.en: One frozen-cloth image stretches from boards and joints to prices and drinks.
normalIntro.cn: 一个「冻硬的抹布」画面可以从木板、关节延伸到价格与烈酒。

normal.en: Stiff and stick differ by one letter: hard or stuck.
normal.cn: stiff 与 stick 只差一个字母：硬或粘。

normal.en: Stiff muscles after exercise is the everyday body sense.
normal.cn: 运动后肌肉发僵是日常身体义。

normal.en: Keep a stiff upper lip is a fixed idiom for staying calm under trouble.
normal.cn: keep a stiff upper lip 是遇事不动声色的固定习语。

normal.en: Stiff competition and a stiff penalty show the harsh side.
normal.cn: stiff competition 与 stiff penalty 体现严苛义。

normal.en: Stiffen is the verb: cold weather stiffens your hands.
normal.cn: 动词是 stiffen：寒冷使手变僵。

abstract.en: Try to bend a board frozen solid and feel it refuse.
abstract.cn: 试着弯折冻硬的木板，感受它纹丝不弯。

abstract.en: Feel your neck refusing to turn on the morning after exercise.
abstract.cn: 体会运动次日早晨脖子转不动的感觉。

abstract.en: Picture a handshake so formal it could crack.
abstract.cn: 想象一个僵硬得几乎会咔咔作响的握手。

examples.en: The old boots were so stiff that they hurt my ankles.
examples.cn: 这双旧靴子硬得磨脚踝。

examples.en: The painting competition draws stiff entries every year.
examples.cn: 绘画比赛每年都竞争激烈。

examples.en: He answered in a stiff voice and left.
examples.cn: 他用生硬的语气回答后就离开了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯迪夫」——谐音「死抵」：冻僵的东西死死抵住，怎么掰都不弯。

root: 源自古英语 stif（僵直坚硬），一般认为上溯至日耳曼语 *stif-（僵硬不弯）；与 stick、still 无词源关系。

sensesIntro.en: From the unbending board grow the frozen joint, the awkward manner, the harsh wind of competition, and the drink that knocks you flat.
sensesIntro.cn: 从折不弯的木板生长出冻僵的关节、生硬的举止、激烈的竞争与一口放倒的烈酒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloth frozen stiff on the window frame that refuses to bend
core.cn: 核心意象：冻在窗框上、掰都掰不动的抹布

branches.en: material that resists bending
branches.cn: 抗拒弯曲的材料

branches.en: the body's joints refusing to move
branches.cn: 身体关节动弹不得

branches.en: a manner frozen into formality
branches.cn: 僵在正式里的举止

branches.en: the harsh force of wind, rules, and drink
branches.cn: 风、规则与酒的严酷冲击力

branches.en: the same resistance in things and bodies
branches.cn: 物与身共享的同一份抗拒

intro.en: Stiff makes a small but useful family around hardness.
intro.cn: stiff 围绕「坚硬」构成一个小而实用的词族。

latinIntro.en: Stiff has no Latin relatives; it is native Germanic, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: stiff 没有拉丁同源词，属日耳曼本土词源，故拉丁同族词列表为空。

items.meaning: in a rigid or formal way
to become rigid, often of the body

items.meaningCN: 刚性的；死板的（正式说法）

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「僵硬地；生硬地」
由形容词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「僵硬；硬度；生硬」
由本词加动词后缀 -en 构成，义为「使变硬；变硬」

definition_zh: 地毯；厚厚一层覆盖物
definition_en: a thick woven material used to cover floors, or a thick layer of something
core_image: 一块厚布把整片地面铺满
scene: 客厅的地板上铺着一块厚地毯。 A thick carpet covered the floor of the living room.
sceneCN: 这里 carpet 是「地毯」（第 1 个义项：铺在地面的厚织物）；句意是客厅的地板上铺着一块厚地毯。

derivatives.zh: carpet 加 -ing 构成，义为「地毯材料；铺地织物」
carpet 加 -ed 构成，义为「铺了地毯的」
carpet 与 bag 复合，义为「旧式旅行毡袋」

senses.title: A thick floor covering
senses.definition: a piece of thick woven material used to cover a floor
senses.definitionCN: 铺在地面上的厚织物
senses.example: The carpet in the hall is old and worn.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅里的地毯又旧又破。
senses.why: The word first named thick woolen cloth, and cloth laid on a floor became a carpet.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指厚毛布，铺在地上的厚布就成了地毯。

senses.title: A thick layer covering a surface
senses.definition: a thick continuous layer of something covering the ground
senses.definitionCN: 厚厚地、连续地盖住地面的一层东西
senses.example: A carpet of fallen leaves covered the path.
senses.exampleCN: 小路上铺满了落叶。
senses.why: A carpet covers a floor completely, so any complete covering can be called a carpet.
senses.whyCN: 地毯把地面整片盖住，因此任何完整覆盖的一层都可以叫 carpet。

intro.en: Carpet goes back to a Latin verb meaning to pluck, because the cloth was made of pulled wool.
intro.cn: carpet 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「撕扯」的动词，因为这种布由扯下的羊毛制成。

items.en: carpere meant to pluck or pull apart, used of wool and fibers.
items.cn: carpere 意为「采摘、扯开」，用于羊毛和纤维。

items.en: carpita named wool or a rough woolen fabric.
items.cn: carpita 指羊毛或粗糙的毛织物。

items.en: carpite named a thick woolen cloth used as a cover.
items.cn: 古法语 carpite 指用作覆盖物的厚毛布。

items.en: English borrowed it as carpet for a table cover, then for a floor covering.
items.cn: 英语借入为 carpet，先指桌布，后指铺地织物。

items.en: The covering sense widened to a carpet of leaves and to carpet as a verb.
items.cn: 覆盖义扩展到「一层落叶」，并产生动词用法。

note.en: Carpet is a cloth word that became a covering word, and it sits beside rug and mat.
note.cn: carpet 由「布」变成「覆盖物」，与 rug、mat 相邻。

entries.definition: material used for making carpets
entries.definitionCN: 制作地毯的材料，由 carpet 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: an old-fashioned travelling bag made of carpet material
entries.definitionCN: 旧式旅行毡袋，由 carpet 与 bag 复合而成。

entries.definition: rough woolen cloth in Latin
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中的粗毛布，是 carpet 的源头。

entries.definition: a small carpet that does not cover the whole floor
entries.definitionCN: 小块地毯，通常不铺满整个地面。

entries.definition: a small flat piece of material laid on a floor
coarse material woven into mats

normalIntro.en: The word comes from plucked wool: rough cloth first, floor covering later.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词来自被扯下的羊毛：先有粗毛布，后有铺地织物。

normal.en: carpet comes from Latin carpere, to pluck, the same root as excerpt.
normal.cn: carpet 来自拉丁语 carpere（摘、扯），与 excerpt 同根。

normal.en: The first carpets were thick woolen cloths laid over tables or floors.
normal.cn: 最早的地毯是铺在桌上或地上的厚毛布。

normal.en: red carpet is the fixed phrase for an official welcome.
normal.cn: red carpet 是「隆重欢迎」的固定说法。

normal.en: a carpet of leaves uses the covering sense with a named material.
normal.cn: a carpet of leaves 用具体材料来表示「覆盖的一层」。

normal.en: As a verb, carpet means to cover a floor completely.
normal.cn: 作动词时，carpet 指把地面整片铺满。

abstract.en: Picture a thick red cloth laid down a staircase step by step.
abstract.cn: 想象一条厚厚的红布沿着楼梯一级级铺下去。

abstract.en: Picture autumn leaves covering a path so completely that no stone shows.
abstract.cn: 想象秋叶把小路盖得严严实实，一块石头都看不见。

abstract.en: Picture bare feet sinking a little into soft wool.
abstract.cn: 想象赤脚陷进柔软羊毛里一点点。

examples.en: A thick carpet covered the floor of the living room.
examples.cn: 客厅的地板上铺着一块厚地毯。

examples.en: The carpet in the hall is old and worn.
examples.cn: 大厅里的地毯又旧又破。

examples.en: A carpet of fallen leaves covered the path.
examples.cn: 小路上铺满了落叶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡皮特」——皮特把厚厚的布卡在地板上，就是地毯。

root: 拉丁语 carpere（撕扯、摘取）→ carpita（羊毛）→ 古法语 carpite（厚毛布）→ 英语 carpet。

sensesIntro.en: A cloth that covers a floor, then any layer that covers a surface.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是一块铺满地面的布，后来指任何铺满表面的层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thick cloth spread until the whole floor disappears.
core.cn: 核心意象：厚布铺开，直到整片地面都不见了。

branches.en: The floor sense: woven material covering a room.
branches.cn: 地面义：覆盖房间地面的织物。

branches.en: The layer sense: leaves, snow, or flowers covering the ground.
branches.cn: 覆盖层义：落叶、雪或花铺满地面。

branches.en: red carpet turns the object into a sign of honour.
branches.cn: red carpet 把物件变成了礼遇的象征。

branches.en: Both senses depend on complete coverage rather than a small patch.
branches.cn: 两个义项都强调「整片盖住」，而不是只铺一小块。

branches.en: The verb carpet extends the same image: to cover a surface thickly.
branches.cn: 动词 carpet 延伸同一画面：厚厚地覆盖一个表面。

intro.en: Carpet is a base noun from Latin; -ing and -ed build its small family.
intro.cn: carpet 是来自拉丁语的基础名词，-ing 与 -ed 构成它不大的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin carpere, to pluck, and carpita, wool, explain the word's origin in pulled fiber.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carpere（扯下）与 carpita（羊毛）说明这个词源于被扯下的纤维。

items.meaning: a thick covering for a floor
items.example: The carpet was cleaned last week.

items.meaning: more than one carpet, or covers thickly
items.meaningCN: carpet 的复数，或动词第三人称单数

items.exampleCN: 他们选了灰色的地毯材料。

items.meaning: an old travelling bag made of carpet cloth
items.exampleCN: 医生提着一个旧式毡袋。

items.example: A rug lay by the fire.
items.exampleCN: 炉火旁铺着一块小地毯。

items.example: Carpere described the pulling of wool.
items.exampleCN: carpere 描写扯下羊毛的动作。

items.example: Carpita is the direct source of carpet.
items.exampleCN: carpita 是 carpet 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 制服；校服；军服；统一的；一律的；一致的
definition_en: the special clothes worn by members of a school, service, or team, or being the same in every part
core_image: 一排学生穿着同一款式同一颜色同一尺码的校服，站成一条整齐的直线
scene: 开学第一天，校门口有位女老师拿着尺子检查每个人的衣领和袖口。 Every student wore the same blue uniform, down to the buttons.
sceneCN: 这里 uniform 是「校服、制服」（第 1 个义项：同一团体成员穿的同款服装）；句意为每个学生都穿着同样的蓝色校服，连纽扣都一样。排成一排的同款衣服，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 均匀的；无变化的（速度、质地）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「一致地；均匀地」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「一致性；一律」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「穿制服的」
由本词加 -less 构成，义为「没有制服的」

senses.title: Clothes that mark a group
senses.definition: a set of clothes that all members of a school, service, or team wear
senses.definitionCN: 某学校、部队或团队的成员全部穿着的成套服装
senses.example: Nurses at the city hospital wear a white uniform.
senses.exampleCN: 市医院的护士穿白色制服。
senses.why: Uni- is one and form is shape: one shape of dress for many bodies.
senses.whyCN: uni- 是「一」，form 是「形状」：许多身体只穿一种形状的衣服。

senses.title: The same in every part
senses.definition: being the same in size, style, or rules everywhere, without variation
senses.definitionCN: 在尺寸、样式或规则上处处相同，没有变化
senses.example: All branches follow a uniform set of safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 所有分店都遵循一套统一的安全规则。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the very image of the clothes: one form applied everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留的正是衣服的意象：一种形式被用到处处。

senses.title: Steady and even
senses.definition: remaining at a constant level or rate, without speeding up or slowing down
senses.definitionCN: 保持在恒定水平或速率上，不快也不慢
senses.example: A falling object moves in nearly uniform acceleration near the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 落体在地面附近几乎做匀加速运动。
senses.why: In physics one form must also mean one rate: nothing in the motion changes shape.
senses.whyCN: 在物理学里，一种形式也要求一种速率：运动中没有任何部分改变样子。

senses.title: To make things alike
senses.definition: to bring parts or rules into one form, so that all are alike
senses.definitionCN: 把各部分或规则归成一种形式，使它们彼此相同
senses.example: The new manager uniformed the labels across the whole warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 新任经理把整个仓库的标签统一了起来。
senses.why: The verb turns the state into an action: someone decides what the one form shall be.
senses.whyCN: 动词把状态变成动作：由某个人来决定那唯一的形式是什么。

senses.title: Members of the service
senses.definition: used with the to mean the police, soldiers, or other people in uniform
senses.definitionCN: 与 the 连用，指警察、士兵或其他穿制服的人
senses.example: The crowd stepped aside quickly when the uniform arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 穿制服的人一到，人群立刻让开。
senses.why: By a familiar shift, the clothing stands for whoever wears it.
senses.whyCN: 衣服代替了穿它的人，这是常见的转义。

intro.en: Uniform joins a Latin word for one to a Latin word for shape, and the pair entered English through French.
intro.cn: uniform 把拉丁语表示「一」的词与表示「形状」的词拼在一起，再经由法语进入英语。

items.en: Unus meant one, and forma meant a shape, mould, or appearance.
items.cn: 拉丁语 unus 意为「一」，forma 意为「形状、模子、外观」。

items.en: Uniformis was used for what keeps a single form, and the schools applied it to evenness of quality.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 uniformis 指保持单一形式的事物，经院学者用它表示质性齐一。

items.en: French uniforme carried both the abstract sense of even and same and, later, the sense of a dress.
items.cn: 法语 uniforme 既有「一律、相同」的抽象义，后来又生出了服装义。

items.en: From the seventeenth century soldiers and servants were dressed alike, and uniform came to mean the dress itself.
items.cn: 十七世纪起士兵与仆役制服整齐，uniform 由此转指这套衣服。

items.en: Schools, hospitals and transport staff adopted uniforms, while science kept the sense of uniform speed and uniform law.
items.cn: 学校、医院与交通部门采用制服，科学界则保留匀速与统一规律的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on uni- and forma; the near-meaning group gathers words for clothing and for sameness with different emphasis.
note.cn: 形近组收以 uni- 与 forma 构成的词；近义组收表示服装与一致性的词，侧重点不同。

entries.definition: The noun for being the same everywhere; the quality behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一致性、一律」，是形容词背后的性质。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in the same way everywhere, or at an even rate.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「一致地、均匀地」。

entries.definition: An adjective for someone who is wearing a uniform.
To make separate parts into one whole; it shares the one part but not the shape.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「统一、使成一体」，共享「一」这一部分而非形状。

entries.definition: A shape or a printed paper; the second half of uniform on its own.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「形状、表格」，即 uniform 的后半部分。

entries.definition: Always the same in behaviour or standard; usually about actions rather than looks.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「一贯的、一致的」，多指行为或标准而非外观。

entries.definition: An agreed level or pattern that things should meet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「标准」，指应达到的既定水平或样式。

entries.definition: A set of clothes worn together, with no idea of group membership.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一套衣服」，不含团体属含义。

entries.definition: The distinctive dress given to servants or staff of a household.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「号衣、仆役制服」，历史上大户人家发给仆人的服装。

entries.definition: An official rule, or the plain clothing required by one, as in regulation dress.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「规定」，也可指规定所要求的朴素服装。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two Latin pieces, one and form, and the ordinary phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用两个拉丁部件「一」与「形」，以及这个词常用的搭配。

normal.en: Uni- means one and form means shape: one shape of clothing for everyone.
normal.cn: uni- 表示「一」，form 表示「形状」：所有人只穿一种形状的衣服。

normal.en: School uniform, military uniform, in uniform: the phrase always marks belonging.
normal.cn: school uniform、military uniform、in uniform：这些搭配都在标记归属。

normal.en: Uniform rules and uniform speed keep one form across space and time.
normal.cn: 统一规则与匀速运动都在空间与时间上保持同一形式。

normal.en: Uniform is also a physics word, as in uniform motion.
normal.cn: uniform 也是物理术语，如匀速运动 uniform motion。

normal.en: The uniform can stand for the person: the crowd quietened when the uniform came.
normal.cn: 制服可以代替人：制服一到，人群就安静了。

abstract.en: Picture many shoulders under cloth cut once: the individual is still there, but the outline is shared.
abstract.cn: 想象许多肩膀罩在同一块剪裁好的布下：个人还在，轮廓却是共享的。

abstract.en: A uniform is a promise made visible: whoever wears it agrees to be seen as one of a group.
abstract.cn: 制服是看得见的承诺：谁穿上它，就同意被看作团体中的一员。

abstract.en: From clothes to rules to speed, the word always asks whether everything really has the same shape.
abstract.cn: 从服装到规则再到速度，这个词始终在问：所有东西真的都是同一个形状吗。

examples.en: He keeps his old army uniform folded in a wooden box.
examples.cn: 他把旧军装叠好放在一只木箱里。

examples.en: The two schools agreed on a uniform exam paper.
examples.cn: 两所学校商定使用统一的试卷。

examples.en: The train moved at a uniform speed along the straight track.
examples.cn: 列车沿笔直的轨道匀速前进。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优尼佛姆」——优尼一人一件佛姆款：统一的制服

root: 源自拉丁语 unus「一」加 forma「形状」，中世纪拉丁语 uniformis 指「保持单一形式、性质齐一」，经法语 uniforme 进入英语，十七世纪起转指统一的服装，科学中也保留「匀速、统一规律」的用法。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of uniform all hold one idea: a single shape imposed on many things, whether clothes, rules, speed, labels, or the people who wear them.
sensesIntro.cn: uniform 的五个义项都守住同一个观念：把单一的形状施加到许多对象上，无论那是衣服、规则、速度、标签，还是穿它的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of students in identical blue clothes with identical buttons.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排学生穿着同样的蓝色衣服，纽扣也一模一样。

branches.en: THE CLOTHES: one cut of cloth worn by a whole group.
branches.cn: 服装线：一整个团体都穿同一种剪裁的布。

branches.en: THE RULES: the same standard applied everywhere without exception.
branches.cn: 规则线：同一标准被无例外地用到处处。

branches.en: THE RATE: in physics the form and the speed must stay one.
branches.cn: 速率线：在物理中形式与速度都必须保持同一。

branches.en: THE ACT: someone brings parts into the one form.
branches.cn: 动作线：由某人把各部分归入那唯一的形式。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: the clothing stands for the person who wears it.
branches.cn: 人物线：衣服代替了穿衣服的人。

intro.en: Uniform is a Latin prefix-root pair with an English suffix family grown on top.
intro.cn: uniform 是一对拉丁语前缀与词根，上面又长出一族英语后缀词。

latinIntro.en: Both unus and forma are recorded Latin words, and uniformis is recorded in medieval Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 unus 与 forma 都有文献记录，uniformis 见于中世纪拉丁语。

items.example: The prefix supplies the idea of oneness.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀提供「唯一」的意思。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「形状」的意思。

items.example: The Latin source of the second half.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分的拉丁语来源。

items.example: The recorded Latin form of the whole word.
items.exampleCN: 整词在中世纪拉丁语中的形式。

items.example: A cousin built on the same prefix.
items.exampleCN: 用同一前缀构成的近亲词。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 具有一种形式的；一律的
